title: Merz to meet Pope Leo, Meloni in Rome
content:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz will meet Pope Leo XIV and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Monday, three officials familiar with the plans told POLITICO.

The visit to the Vatican, Merz’s first private audience with the pope, is set to focus on human dignity, artificial intelligence and efforts to bring peace to Ukraine, two of the officials said.

Merz also plans to meet Cardinal Secretary of State Pietro Parolin, the Vatican’s top diplomat, who in September used his U.N. General Assembly speech to call for an immediate ceasefire in Ukraine and a path to diplomacy.

A German government spokesperson declined to comment, saying the chancellor’s trips are announced on the Friday of the preceding week.

Merz, a Catholic, attended Leo’s inauguration in May 2025 but did not meet the pontiff in private. Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul met Parolin at the Vatican in early October for talks that also covered AI, the war in Ukraine and Black Sea grain exports.

title: Picking up the mic: A speaker’s experience from Wiki Indaba 2026
content:
In my mind I was preparing for an unexpected turn, as this was my first conference with Wikimedia. I got a scholarship to attend the 2026 Wiki Indaba and my plan was to just be a part of the audience through every session within the three days. That changed as I got a last-minute invitation to step in for a colleague from the Wikimedia Kenya User Group who had proposed a lightning talk that got approved but was unable to secure a scholarship to travel.

The lightning talk on growing Swahili Wikipedia: the lessons from Kenya’s translation model happened on the third day of the conference.

The lightning talk was based on a common challenge faced by different indigenous African languages in scaling their editions of Wikipedia: ‘How do we scale digital knowledge in under-represented languages without overwhelming new editors?’

What we realized back in Kenya is that one of the biggest hurdles wasn’t a lack of language fluency or enthusiasm but the belief that Wikimedia tools were too technical. To test this, we trained over thirty volunteers on using the translation tool for Swahili content. We walked them through using the content translation tool and paired them with experienced peers.

title: “Freezer hackers” have also targeted Latvia – terrorism or vandalism?
content:
Media reports have speculated about the involvement of Russian intelligence services, but Kirils Solovjovs, head of the IT security company group Possible Security, told Delfi that the perpetrators could just as easily be ordinary vandals exploiting the capabilities of artificial intelligence and businesses’ lack of cybersecurity awareness. Meanwhile, Madara Krutova, a representative of CERT.lv, which monitors Latvia’s internet security, told Delfi that so far only one warehouse in Latvia has been affected, while a further 300 potential threats have been identified and prevented in time.

The first large-scale attack on various refrigeration systems by hackers whose identities remain unknown came to media attention in early October, when malicious actors remotely accessed freezers in French supermarkets and set their desired temperature to +50°C. Some freezers even caught fire as a result.

title: Greece ditched coal in 15 years. The rest of Europe could learn from it
content:
Greece has shown that ditching coal need not be painful. Just 15 years ago, coal accounted for more than half of its electricity generation. Today, only one coal-fired unit remains, with gas, wind, solar and hydropower taking its place. Could Greece offer a blueprint for the rest of the EU?

As Greek Minister of Environment and Energy Stavros Papastavrou acknowledges, the southern European country is still recovering from the consequences of the financial crisis that hit in the first half of the previous decade. Despite this, it is pressing ahead with ambitious energy projects, often with financial support from the European Union. These include a subsea cable to Egypt, imports of natural gas from the eastern Mediterranean and connecting the Greek islands to the mainland electricity grid.

Speaking to journalists, Minister Papastavrou said that Crete and the Cyclades islands had already been connected to the mainland grid. Other islands are due to follow in the coming years.

title: ”Huolestuttava käännös oikealle” – näin SDP:n vaihtoehtoa arvostellaan
content:
SDP:n vaihtoehtobudjetti herättää kritiikkiä. Vasemmistoliiton, keskustan ja kokoomuksen edustajat arvostelevat budjetin veroratkaisuja ja niiden vaikutuksia pienituloisiin, yrittäjiin sekä maa- ja metsätalouteen.

Vasemmistoliiton puheenjohtaja Minja Koskela pitää SDP:n tänään julkaisemaa vaihtoehtobudjettia ”huolestuttavana käännöksenä oikealle”.

– SDP haluaa keventää verotusta jopa yli 8000 euron kuukausituloilla, mutta ei perua suurimpia sosiaaliturvan leikkauksia. Toisin sanoen sosialidemokraattien vaihtoehto palkitsee kansanedustajien tulotasolla, mutta ei anna köyhimmille suomalaisille juuri mitään, Koskela sanoo tiedotteessa.

SDP:n vaihtoehtobudjetti lisäisi eduskunnan tietopalvelun laskelmien mukaan 8000 euroa kuukaudessa ansaitsevien nettoansioita 38 eurolla kuukaudessa suhteessa pysyvään lainsäädäntöön. Keskimääräistä ansiopäivärahaa saavan työttömän tulot puolestaan laskisivat 12 eurolla.

Koskela arvostelee SDP:tä indeksijäädytysten hyväksymisestä. Niiden myötä monien pienituloisten ostovoima heikkenee ensi vuonna, hän kritisoi.

PÄÄMINISTERI, kokoomuksen puheenjohtaja Petteri Orpo katsoo, että SDP:n vaihtoehtobudjetti pysäyttäisi Suomen talouden kasvun.

title: Mitä tapahtuu vanhoilla kaatopaikoilla, kun yhdyskuntajätteet muhivat maan kerroksissa? – Jätekukko kehitti mittausvälineen selvitystyöhön
content:
Kaatopaikoilla syntyy metaania vielä vuosikymmeniä sen jälkeen, kun jätteiden loppusijoittaminen on päättynyt. Karkeasti ajateltuna sekajätteeseen aikanaan heitetyt banaaninkuoret aiheuttavat edelleen päästöjä syvällä maan sisässä. Kaatopaikan hapettomissa olosuhteissa orgaaninen jäte hajoaa ja muodostaa muun muassa metaania ja hiilidioksidia sekä rikkivetyä.

Kuopion Heinälamminrinteen jätekeskuksessa kaasujen muodostumista ja talteenottoa on tutkittu osana KAJASTUS-hanketta. Hankkeessa kehitetään menetelmiä, joilla voidaan vähentää metaanipäästöjä, lisätä talteen saatavan kaatopaikkakaasun määrää ja parantaa suljettujen kaatopaikkojen seurantaa.

Suljettukin kaatopaikka elää

Orgaanisen jätteen sijoittamista kaatopaikoille rajoitettiin Suomessa merkittävästi vuonna 2016. Kuopion seudun sekajätteet sijoitettiin pääsääntöisesti kaatopaikalle ennen kuin Riikinvoiman ekovoimalaitos aloitti toimintansa samana vuonna.

Suljettu eli käytöstä poistettu kaatopaikka peitetään esimerkiksi savi- tai muovikerroksilla, jotka lähtökohtaisesti pitävät kaatopaikkakaasut kurissa. Jätemassan painuminen ja liikkuminen voi kuitenkin synnyttää vuotoja etenkin kaivojen, putkien ja muiden läpivientien kohdalle.

title: Landmines: New Use, Production Undermine Ban Treaty
content:
(Geneva, November 24, 2026) – New use, production, and acquisition of antipersonnel landmines contributed to killing or injuring at least 6,929 people in 2025, which is the highest annual total since 2020, Human Rights Watch said today with the release of the “Landmine Monitor 2026” by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines. Human Rights Watch is a founding member of the campaign and contributed to the report.

The 200-page report examines global compliance with the 1997 Mine Ban Treaty and the challenges facing the treaty nearly three decades after its adoption. The treaty comprehensively bans antipersonnel mines and commits countries to eliminate stockpiled weapons, clear contaminated land, and assist mine victims and affected communities.

“At a time when civilian casualties are rising and new technologies make mines easier to deploy, supporting the Mine Ban Treaty is more important than ever,” said Verity Coyle, deputy crisis, conflict and arms director at Human Rights Watch. “All countries should join the treaty, and members should fully uphold its obligations.”

title: Right-wing revolt threatens to bog down EU budget
content:
BRUSSELS — The far-right Patriots for Europe group plans to challenge the European Parliament’s negotiating mandates on several files in the EU’s next budget, according to four EU officials with knowledge of the discussions — a move that could drag out discussions on the seven-year plan in the chamber.

The challenge would stop the files, which have already been discussed at a committee level, from going straight to talks with national governments. Instead, the mandates would need a plenary vote, opening the door to amendments that could rehash positions committees had already settled.

“The merger of several programs [in several budget proposals] is accompanied by an increasing concentration of allocation authority in the hands of the Commission,” a PfE official told POLITICO. Moreover, most of the PfE’s amendments in the budget have been rejected, they said.

The official added that “several delegations outside of the PfE” have told them they would support the challenge.

title: Scoring a Goal for Free Knowledge: How WikiSport’s Football Project Transformed Uzbek Football Coverage on Wikipedia
content:
In Uzbekistan, football isn’t just a pastime–it’s a national obsession. Yet for years, fans searching for reliable, structured information in Uzbek about their own domestic leagues, historic clubs, or local players often hit a dead end. Articles on the Uzbek Wikipedia were either missing entirely or consisted of little more than a single stub sentence.

Launched as a specialized thematic track under the broader WikiStipendiya marathon, the WikiSport: Football project set out to change that. Open to contributors of all backgrounds regardless of where they live, the initiative combined grassroots community editing with institutional sports partnerships to build an encyclopedic archive of Uzbek football from the ground up.

Rather than relying solely on scattered online summaries, editors used these connections and authoritative sports journalism to systematically document decades of post-independence football history-turning the project page into both a coordination hub and a living index of Uzbek football knowledge.

title: Poland is not ready for war with Russia. And NATO’s Article 5 is no automatic guarantee of military intervention
content:
Karolina Zbytniewska, FocusEurope.pl: Are we at war?

Marek Magierowski: With Russia? Yes, we are.

People usually refer to it as hybrid warfare.

We should be very careful about using the term “hybrid warfare”. There is no doubt that Russia has stepped up this kind of activity. During the Cold War, the Russians called it aktivnyye meropriyatiya – active measures, as they were known in the West.

Historically, Russia has always been particularly effective on this front. It has deployed a whole range of tactics to influence different aspects of life in Western Europe and the United States. Today, it is using the same playbook, albeit with the latest technology at its disposal.

While Russia’s war in Ukraine is not going particularly well, to put it mildly, its so-called hybrid operations are proving remarkably effective.

Why should we be wary of using the term?

Because “hybrid warfare” can become a convenient excuse for Western and American politicians and policymakers to avoid taking decisive action in response.

title: Survival vs. combat: Freedom of movement in High North becomes logistics problem
content:
Snow-bound Nordic forces risk stalling. The EU’s Military Mobility Package will help, but cannot fix the issue alone.

In the High North, movement is never guaranteed. Snow, ice, and steep terrain turn short distances into obstacles. Freezing temperatures challenge vehicles, equipment, and the people who rely on them. The harder test is not reaching a destination. It is staying mobile, supplied, and effective; all this far from anything you would normally call infrastructure.

You have to be able to switch from wheels to tracks on the field, even if it’s minus 10 degrees.
— Lt Col David Bonne, French High Mountain Military School Bonne

title: EIT: Välineellistettyä maahantuloa saa torjua – jopa turvapaikanhakua rajoittamalla
content:
Euroopan ihmisoikeustuomioistuin (EIT) on ottanut sallivan kannan Puolan, Liettuan ja Latvian ratkaisuihin turvapaikanhakijoiden pakkopalauttamisesta.

Maat katsoivat vuosina 2021-2022 joutuneensa Valko-Venäjän välineellistetyn maahantulon kohteeksi, ja työnsivät rajan laittomasti ylittäneitä ihmisiä takaisin ilman turvapaikanhakumenettelyä.

Tämä rikkoi valittajien mielestä maiden allekirjoittamia ihmisoikeussopimuksia. Nyt EIT on tehnyt asiassa merkittäväksi kuvatun periaatepäätöksen.

EIT:N MIELESTÄ EU-mailla on tällaisissa vihamielisten valtioiden tarkoituksellisesti järjestämissä kampanjoissa oikeus suojella itseään ja turvallisuussyistä sulkea rajansa.

Joissain tapauksissa turvapaikanhaunkin voi pysäyttää, eikä teko sinänsä riko kansainvälisiä ihmisoikeussopimuksia.

Puola ja Latvia toimivat kuitenkin EIT:n mielestä väärin, koska palautetuissa oli erityistä suojelua tarvitsevia ihmisiä kuten lapsia.

Liettua sen sijaan saa toiminnastaan puhtaat paperit: takaisin siirretyt olivat aikuisia ja terveitä ihmisiä.

PÄÄTÖS on EU-maiden rajaturvallisuuden ja politiikan kannalta tärkeä.

title: Croatia: Border Pushbacks of Adults, Children Violate Rights
content:
(Brussels, November 24, 2026) – Croatian authorities routinely engage in pushbacks at the border, including of unaccompanied children and families with young children, despite European Union efforts to end the practice, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today. 

The 43-page report, “Doing Europe’s Dirty Work: Ongoing Violent Pushbacks of Migrants from Croatia to Bosnia and Herzegovina,” finds that Croatian authorities routinely engage in pushbacks, often violently. An EU-funded Croatian border monitoring program has had little impact on Croatian police pushbacks. Instead, the EU has increased funding to Croatia for border management without addressing the abuse at the border.

title: ‘It’s just a circus’: Founders clash with notaries over new EU startup law
content:
BRUSSELS — Europe’s plan to help startups compete with Silicon Valley has hit an obstacle in the continent’s most buttoned-up profession: notaries.

Unveiled in March as Europe’s answer to Delaware, the European Commission’s EU Inc. proposal would give new companies a quick way to set up a single EU legal entity, sparing them legal advice and form filling in multiple countries. It would also cut notaries out of key stages in a company’s life cycle, a move that has excited startups and rankled the profession.

“It’s just a circus,” said Mihai Streza, a Berlin-based entrepreneur, who sees hefty notary bills and mandatory in-person appointments as emblematic of what Europe gets wrong about startups.

Pushback by the notaries, however, is now complicating negotiations over the proposed regulation, which would create a single company form allowing startups to register online within 48 hours for €100. EU leaders set the end of this year as the deadline for a political deal, but talks between the Parliament and EU countries have yet to start.

title: CDIF progress: new profiles and roadmap coming soon!
content:
Developments on the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) have been moving rapidly since the release of version 1.1 and the launch of the CDIF4EOSC project in June 2026. Work has been focused on both immediate- and longer-term objectives, in a variety of areas. Chief among these are the new profiles under development, a long-running process which is now bearing fruit. Efforts to support the further development of cross-domain metadata models at W3C are on-going, and there are developments in terms of tools, maintenance, and training. The recent workshop ‘Optimising Metadata Structures for Alignments with Standard Models at the Point of Use’ at the Leibniz Foundation’s Schloss Dagstuhl in Wadern, Germany saw many of these activities come to a head.

title: Op-ed | Climate Security Requires Scientific Diplomacy Beyond Geopolitical Tensions
content:
Drawing on fifteen years of experience working at the intersection of science and diplomacy, including a long-running scientific collaboration with North Korea, James Hammond explores the diplomatic and soft-power value of scientific partnerships, the risks posed by their disruption and why protecting them should be considered a national and international security priority.

Climate change is increasingly recognised as a national security threat. Recent statements by the Prime Minister at COP31[1] in Türkiye and the Foreign Secretary at the UN General Assembly[2], together with the appointment of Dame Madeline Alessandri as the world’s first Special Representative for Climate Security, reflect that growing awareness. Yet one aspect receives far less attention: climate security depends upon international scientific collaboration. As geopolitical tensions rise and scientific ties come under increasing pressure, protecting those collaborations should itself be viewed as a security imperative.

The celebration featured an online session followed by an in-person gathering, bringing community members together to appreciate Wikidata’s contributions to free and open knowledge.

The activities provided an opportunity for members to learn more about Wikidata, understand its importance within the Wikimedia movement, and celebrate its impact through creativity and community engagement.

For the Igala Wikimedia Community, the celebration was not just about marking another year in Wikidata’s journey. It was also an opportunity to deepen members’ understanding of the project and reflect on how the community can contribute to building a more connected and inclusive knowledge base.

The celebration began with an online gathering on 23 October 2026. The virtual session provided an opportunity for community members to come together, connect with one another, and celebrate Wikidata’s 14th anniversary.

title: Blogi: Vahva Eurooppa keskittyy olennaiseen
content:
Euroopan unionin budjetista keskusteltaessa huomio kiinnittyy helposti yhteen kysymykseen: kuinka suuri budjetin pitäisi olla? Olennaisempi kysymys on kuitenkin se, mitä yhteisillä euroilla saadaan aikaan.

Eurooppa elää perusteellisesti muuttuneessa maailmassa. Venäjän hyökkäyssota on palauttanut turvallisuuden politiikan keskiöön. Kansainvälinen kilpailu teknologiasta, investoinneista ja raaka-aineista kiristyy. Samalla meidän on vahvistettava Euroopan taloutta, huolehdittava ulkorajojemme turvallisuudesta ja tuettava Ukrainaa pitkäjänteisesti.

Näihin haasteisiin yksikään jäsenmaa ei pysty vastaamaan yksin. Siksi tarvitsemme Euroopan unionia ja yhteistä eurooppalaista budjettia.

EU-myönteisyys ei kuitenkaan tarkoita sitä, että jokainen budjetin kasvattamista koskeva esitys pitäisi hyväksyä. Todellista eurooppalaista vastuunkantoa on huolehtia siitä, että yhteiset varat käytetään tavoitteisiin, joissa yhteistyö tuottaa enemmän vaikuttavuutta kuin jäsenmaiden toiminta erikseen.

title: Grant OPUS LAP dla prof. Bartosza Pielińskiego na badania nad samoregulacją AI w społecznościach otwartych zasobów cyfrowych
content:
Z przyjemnością informujemy, że dr hab. Bartosz Pieliński, prof. UW, związany z naszą Katedrą UNESCO, otrzymał finansowanie w prestiżowym konkursie OPUS 30 LAP/Weave Narodowego Centrum Nauki (NCN). Jego projekt pt. „Zmiana reguł, norm i strategii związanych ze wspólnymi zasobami otwartego oprogramowania i otwartej treści w wyniku pojawienia się dużych modeli językowych” (Changing Rules, Norms and Strategies of the Open Source and Open Content Commons Following the Emergence of Large Language Models) poświęcony jest temu, w jaki sposób społeczności internetowe samodzielnie wypracowują zasady korzystania z narzędzi sztucznej inteligencji.

Projekt koncentruje się na dwóch typach społeczności, na które rozwój generatywnej sztucznej inteligencji wywiera szczególnie istotny wpływ: społecznościach rozwijających otwarte oprogramowanie (open source) oraz tworzących otwarte zasoby treści (open content). Badania obejmą m.in. społeczności skupione wokół rozwoju Linuksa i Wikipedii, analizując, jak reagują one na upowszechnienie narzędzi opartych na dużych modelach językowych (LLM).

title: Citing Trafficking Risks, Georgia Plans Total Ban on Surrogacy
content:
Georgia’s ruling party has announced plans to impose a complete ban on surrogacy, framing the move as a campaign against human trafficking and the exploitation of women, even as opposition leaders and fertility doctors accused the government of bowing to the Orthodox Church and threatening families struggling with infertility.

Irakli Kirtskhalia, a lawmaker with the governing Georgian Dream party, said after a meeting of the parliamentary majority that legislation was being drafted to outlaw the practice entirely, though in vitro fertilization would remain legal. Georgia’s surrogacy market has expanded significantly since 2023, Kirtskhalia said, adding that the party had consulted both executive authorities and the Georgian Patriarchate.

“We understand well that banning surrogacy may have a certain economic impact; however, we believe that economic benefits cannot outweigh these risks and ethical issues,” he said.

title: Civil society questions decree that could block access to telecommunications networks in Mozambique
content:
Officials claim the measure ‘protects society,’ but civil society organizations see a threat to freedom of expression

Originally published on Global Voices Advox

Post-election protests in Maputo, Mozambique, in 2025. Photo by Wilson Thole. Used with permission.

Civil society organizations in Mozambique, such as the Center for Democracy and Human Rights (CDD), submitted a document to the Ombudsman contesting the constitutionality of Decree No. 48/2025, issued in December 2025, which establishes control mechanisms and potential blocks on access to telecommunications networks in the country.

According to the portal Moz24h, journalists and experts are concerned that the measure could threaten rights such as freedom of expression, access to information, and communication, particularly in contexts of social mobilization or political tension. The challenge arises in an environment still heated from the conflicts following the 2024 elections.

title: Statement zum Innenausschuss: AlgorithmWatch warnt vor Fiasko bei KI-Migrationsverwaltungsgesetz
content:
Berlin, 23. November 2026 – Heute berät der Innenausschuss des Deutschen Bundestags über den Entwurf für das KI-Migrationsverwaltungsgesetz (KIMVG). Mit dem Gesetz soll Migrationsbehörden erlaubt werden, KI-Systeme mit Daten aus Visums- und Asylverfahren entwickeln und einsetzen zu dürfen. Bereits vergangene Woche hat AlgorithmWatch mit 36 weiteren Organisationen einen gemeinsamen Appell unterzeichnet und darin konkrete Nachbesserungen in den Bereichen Datenschutz, Evaluation und Transparenz gefordert. Darüber hinaus kritisiert AlgorithmWatch, dass der jetzige Gesetzentwurf zu vielen Behörden erlaubt, beim Einsatz von KI Grundrechte einzuschränken.

Nora Oppermann, Junior Policy Managerin bei AlgorithmWatch, kommentiert:

„Das KIMVG soll einem kaum begrenzten Behördenkreis ermöglichen, mit hochsensiblen Daten eigene KI-Systeme zu entwickeln. Dazu zählen 225 Auslandsvertretungen, 585 kommunale Ausländerbehörden und sämtliche Dienststellen der Polizei. Zwischen touristischen Visa aus Nordamerika und Asylgesuchen von geflüchteten Menschen aus Kriegs- und Krisengebieten wird dabei kein Unterschied gemacht.

title: Durchleuchtet – Anatomie eines Roboters
content:
Was steckt eigentlich in einem humanoiden Roboter? Um das herauszufinden, muss er nicht auseinandergenommen werden. Für dieses Projekt wurde der Roboter Oli im Kepler Universitätsklinikum einer Computertomographie (CT) unterzogen.

Die Aufnahmen machen sein Inneres sichtbar und geben Einblick in eine technische Blackbox, die normalerweise verborgen bleibt. Dabei zeigt sich: Auch wenn Oli äußerlich an den menschlichen Körper erinnert, besteht sein Innenleben aus Motoren, Kabeln und elektronischen Bauteilen. Seine Konstruktion orientiert sich in ihrer Form am menschlichen Körper, folgt im Inneren aber ganz eigenen Prinzipien. 

Credit:
Prof. Franz Fellner, Daniel Schneeweiß, Kepler Universitätsklinikum (KUK) Linz

title: China Sends Post-Shenzhen Signals to Europe
content:
Europe was left out of the Shenzhen summit, but it wasn’t forgotten, at least in Chinese minds. The state media was quick to send signals that it was thinking of Europe (which in turn has been thinking of targeting Chinese imports).

Xi Jinping’s November 19 appearance with US President Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, the Russian leader, ended with a statement speaking of peace and co-operation in broad terms.

There was little for diplomats to get their teeth into beyond the images of the US and Chinese leaders standing together, accompanied by the head of a lesser Eurasian power. Europe was absent, and yet Beijing’s messaging suggests it still matters a great deal.

The Chinese party-state is adept at using its coordinated media outlets for coded dispatches in the absence of official position-taking. As initial clues to what comes next, these are worth noting because they serve as a guide to official thinking.

title: Brussels wants greener fishing. Its own rules are standing in the way
content:
Outdated EU rules are preventing fishers from modernising their fleets and investing in cleaner technology, national governments warn. They are calling for more ambitious reforms than Brussels is currently willing to offer.

European governments are urging Brussels to revise fishing rules that they say prevent the modernisation of fishing businesses. The EU Commission, however, has opted to take a partial approach to revision. The debate emerged during the Council meeting where ministers assessed the Commission Vision 2040 for fisheries and aquaculture.

The goal of the Vision is to protect the EU marine ecosystems, boost seafood production and support coastal communities. But several countries said these goals are meaningless unless actual changes were made to the rules.

European Commission’s Vision 2040 identifies its priorities for the next 15 years. These include cleaner fishing vessels, stronger support for small-scale fishers and increased public investment in aquaculture.

title: Your boss may not be ready to manage AI
content: If you have an office job, chances are you’ve had at least one earnest chat about how AI could streamline your work. Across Europe, 67% of companies are already using generative AI tools, while another 13% plan to do so in the next year. In a 2025 survey more than 70% of Europeans said they felt AI could improve their productivity, while at the same time overwhelmingly supporting safeguards to ensure its responsible use in the workplace. “You can have good principles, but who is responsible for implementing them inside companies?” asked Maxime Legrand, president of the European managers trade union association CEC. “In practice, that’s managers.” Yet much is still unknown about how AI is actually being used in the workplace. That's why his organisation is collaborating with the Technical University of Munich on a study examining how companies are adopting and managing the technology. title: Baltic Sea Region Youth Survey 2027: young people, tell us what matters to you
content:
The Baltic Sea Region Youth Forum (BSRYF) launches a region-wide survey on what matters to young people of age 16-30, and how much they trust politics. The survey is open until 14 December 2026.

How do young people in the Baltic Sea Region see their role in politics and society? The Baltic Sea Region Youth Forum (BSRYF), an independent body of young people supported by the Council of the Baltic Sea States (CBSS), has launched the Baltic Sea Region Youth Survey 2027 to find out.

The survey is open to young people in Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Poland and Sweden and available in all languages. It has four parts:

  • Regional relevance: how much eight topics matter to young people personally and for cooperation in the region, including climate protection, security and resilience, education and economic opportunities, migration, digital transformation, and infrastructure and mobility, and how much say they feel they have on each.
  • Trust in politics: whether young people feel represented, listened to and taken seriously by politicians.
  • Participation in practice: which forms of participation young people use, would consider, and can realistically access.

title: Spotted on the D.C. Metro: Trump Staffer Accidentally Reveals Plan for Smithsonian Overhaul
content:
Since the Trump administration erupted this summer with criticism of the Smithsonian National Museum of American History for promoting “radical activist ideology” and precipitated the planned departure of Smithsonian secretary Lonnie Bunch, the White House’s next step on this front of the culture wars has been unclear.

Now the plan may have been revealed — inadvertently — in a crowded car on Washington, D.C.’s Metro transit system.

In the last week of October, as political Washington was focused on the coming midterm elections, a commuter on the Orange Line from the Northern Virginia suburbs was startled to see displayed, on the laptop of a man seated adjacent in a gray tartan suit, a document titled “Smithsonian Institution Renewal Plan.” The commuter snapped a few phone photos over the man’s shoulder and dispatched them to ProPublica.

If you see something in public you think ProPublica should know about, there are a few ways you can reach us securely.

title: Political Prisoner Spotlight: Idris Khattak and the Persecution of Human Rights Defenders in Pakistan
content:
Register 


Human rights defender Idris Khattak spent decades documenting human rights violations, including enforced disappearances, in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province and the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas. In retaliation for this work, he was abducted, disappeared, tortured, and sentenced to 14 years in prison. His ongoing detention highlights how the Pakistani authorities have used extralegal means to silence criticism, deployed national security legislation against perceived opponents, relied on military courts to try civilians, and endangered the lives of political prisoners through mistreatment and medical neglect.

To mark the seven-year anniversary of Idris Khattak’s detention, Freedom House is hosting a virtual event that will discuss the current status of the case, what it reveals about the persecution of human rights defenders in Pakistan more broadly, and how democratic governments and multilateral institutions can respond.

Speakers Include: 

  • Hina Jilani, human rights lawyer and member of The Elders
  • Talia Khattak, daughter of Idris Khattak
  • Laura Rosenberger, executive vice president, Freedom House

content:

  • A drone attack, suspected to have been launched by the Ethiopian National Defence Forces (ENDF), hit a vehicle in Adi Hara, Biyara kebele, Tahtay Adiyabo woreda, North-Western Tigray zone. At least four civilians were injured in the attack.

title: ”I can do it” – Digitaidot avaavat uusia mahdollisuuksia Zimbabwen nuorille naisille
content:
Milicent Gumbiran, 20, tarina on Zimbabwessa tyypillinen. 

Hänen perheensä ajautui taloudellisiin ongelmiin isän kuoleman jälkeen, ja hän jätti 17-vuotiaana lukion kesken juuri ennen loppukokeita. Viiden lapsen koulumaksut olivat yksinhuoltajaäidille liikaa. 

“Oli tuskallista selviytyä. Joinakin päivinä menimme nukkumaan ilman ruokaa. Se oli hyvin vaikeaa äidilleni ja meille lapsille”, Gumbira kertoo. 

Zimbabwessa koulutuksen loppuun saaminen ei ole itsestäänselvyys, ja vaikka koulutodistuksen saisi käteensä, siirtyminen koulunpenkiltä palkkatyöhön on nuorille vaikeaa tai jopa mahdotonta. Virallisia työpaikkoja on vähän, eivätkä työnhakijoiden taidot usein vastaa työnantajien vaatimuksiin esimerkiksi digitaitojen osalta.  

Zimbabwe on kärsinyt koko 2000-luvun ajan taloudellisesta epävakaudesta sekä lisääntyneestä köyhyydestä. Afrikan kehityspankin mukaan vuonna 2026 noin 40 prosenttia väestöstä elää köyhyysrajan alapuolella (alle kahdella dollarilla päivässä). Zimbabwen tilastokeskuksen mukaan 15–24-vuotiaista noin 48 prosenttia on työvoiman ja koulutuksen ulkopuolella.

title: Interés menguante, desconfianza y polarización: Así se informan los españoles
content:
Los españoles están llamados a votar en las elecciones generales de este domingo. Los sondeos sugieren que Pedro Sánchez, que ha gobernado el país desde 2018, podría perder el poder. Las elecciones son un buen momento para explorar cómo los españoles se informan con la ayuda de más de una década de datos del Digital News Report.

Nuestros datos muestran que las audiencias más jóvenes tienen menos confianza y menos interés en las noticias, y son las más propensas a usar chatbots y redes sociales para informarse. La confianza en la radiotelevisión pública divide profundamente a los españoles, la preocupación por la desinformación en línea está en su punto más alto y muchos critican la cobertura que los medios hacen del clima y la inmigración. A continuación, presentamos nueve hallazgos de nuestro informe.

title: Cop31: Why the UN climate summit ended in victory for fossil fuel producing nations
content:
The UN’s annual two-week climate summit, Cop31, has ended in failure. Countries could not find consensus on a final agreement. It is the first such failure in more than 20 years.

The summit started relatively smoothly. In fact, the conference agenda was adopted within a few hours on day one, as country parties found nothing objectionable. At the time, this event looked like it might be smooth sailing: another summit simply focused on implementing policies agreed in previous years.

But week two became explosive. First, the draft agreement – which if adopted would have been known as the Antalya Accords – conceded that we have failed to keep global temperature rise below 1.5˚C and that the world is entering a period of “overshoot”. Second, oil and gas producing nations fought to keep the root cause of climate change – namely fossil fuels – out of any deal. And they succeeded, as the agreement fell through.

title: PNG’s parliament is voting on ratifying Bougainville independence. A ‘no’ won’t be the end of the story
content:
After more than a century of struggle, Bougainville is moving closer to becoming the world’s newest nation. An autonomous region of Papua New Guinea (PNG) in the northern Solomon Islands chain, Bougainville is taking its next step toward self-determination after a decade-long civil war and a 25-year peace process.

In a 2019 referendum, almost 98% of Bougainvilleans voted for independence. Today the parliament of PNG will begin to vote on ratifying that result.

A “yes” vote in parliament, if it comes, won’t immediately make Bougainville independent. But it will set the legal machinery moving.

Hard questions such as the future of the island’s contentious Panguna mine remain unresolved, but the vote offers a chance to recognise decades of work from the Bougainvillean and PNG sides that have kept the peace process on track.

Bougainville was named by French navigator Louis Antoine de Bougainville in the 18th century, and colonialism has shaped its history ever since. In 1899, it was incorporated into German New Guinea, while the neighbouring Solomon Islands became a British protectorate.

title: Vasemmistopopulistiset demokraattitähdet pyrkivät yhdistämään kansan oligarkiaa vastaan
content:
Yhä useampaa suosittua demokraattipoliitikkoa voi luonnehtia vasemmistopopulistiksi. Vasemmistopopulististen demokraattien suosio heijastaa niin laajaa tyytymättömyyttä vallitsevaan järjestykseen kuin kyllästymistä kahtiajakoja vahvistavaan kulttuurisotimiseen. Mikäli demokraatit onnistuvat populismillaan valjastamaan ihmisten tyytymättömyyden entistäkin tehokkaammin omaksi edukseen, voi heillä vuonna 2029 olla lähes ainutlaatuinen mahdollisuus muuttaa Yhdysvaltoja.

Texasin kuvernööriksi valittu demokraatti Gina Hinojosa totesi ennen 3. marraskuuta pidettyjä välivaaleja ihmisten olevan kyllästyneitä kulttuurisotiin, joista ovat hänen mukaansa hyötyneet ainoastaan teknojätit ja miljardöörit. Demokraattien ”sininen tsunami” osoittaa talouspopulistiksi itseään kutsuvan Hinojosan olleen pitkälti oikeassa, mutta liikaa johtopäätelmiä etenkin presidentti Donald Trumpin epäsuosiota heijastavasta välivaalituloksesta ei pidä vetää.

content:
UN Womenin uuden, 54 maata kattavan Access to Justice for Women Survivors of Violence -tilastokatsauksen mukaan vain joka neljäs (23 %) fyysistä tai seksuaalista väkivaltaa elämänsä aikana kokenut nainen hakee minkäänlaista apua perheeltään, yhteisöltään tai viranomaisilta. title: Katalonian separatistijohtaja Carles Puigdemontin armahdus vahvistettiin
content:
Espanjan korkein oikeus on vahvistanut lopullisesti Katalonian alueen entisen johtajan Carles Puigdemontin armahduksen vuoden 2017 epäonnistuneeseen itsenäistymisyritykseen liittyvistä rikoksista. Viime viikolla tehty päätös julkaistiin maanantaina.

Espanjan korkein oikeus linjasi alun perin toissa vuonna, ettei Puigdemont ollut oikeutettu armahdukseen, koska häntä vastaan oli nostettu myös kavallussyytteet. Puigdemont kuitenkin valitti päätöksestä perustuslakituomioistuimeen, joka päätti viime viime kuussa, että armahdus koski myös kavallussyytteitä. Perustuslakituomioistuimen päätöksestä ei voi enää valittaa.

Espanjan parlamentti hyväksyi Puigdemontin armahduksen vuonna 2024. Armahdus oli osa pääministeri Pedro Sanchezin katalaanipuolueiden kanssa tekemää sopimusta, joka mahdollisti Sanchezin pysymisen vallassa edellisten parlamenttivaalien jälkeen.

title: University Approves Nuclear Weapons Data Center, Township Vows to Fight On
content:
Last week, the University of Michigan’s board of regents approved the construction of a $1.25 billion data center that will power American nuclear weapons research. The regents voted 7 - 1 in a public meeting on November 19 to move forward with the project despite widespread opposition from faculty, staff, and the residents of Ypsilanti Township, Michigan where the data center will operate. A few hours after the vote, the leaders and citizens of the Township gathered to discuss how to stop it.

U of M and Los Alamos National Laboratories (LANL) first announced plans to build what the University then called an “AI research facility” in 2024. U of M now calls the project a “research computing center” and, if all goes to its plan, construction will begin on a 125,000 square foot facility in late 2027. The data center could expand to “no more than 300,000 square feet,” according to a U of M blog post.

During the regent’s meeting, faculty, staff, and members of the community shared their thoughts on the data center’s construction.

title: Nuestros datos, nuestras reglas: Gobernanza de datos para bienes comunes digitales en la era de la IA
content:
Esta pieza fue escrita por Patricia Díaz, coordinadora de la Alianza A2K Latinoamérica y Franco Giandana, analista de políticas públicas en América Latina y el Caribe para Access Now.

Desarrollar un sistema de inteligencia artificial requiere muchos datos, que los principales desarrolladores recopilan de la web, sin compensar ni reconocer a las personas y comunidades que los crean, organizan y custodian. Estos datos se emplean para entrenar sistemas de IA, es decir, para reconocer patrones o generar respuestas. Esta extracción masiva de datos es  una forma de explotación de los bienes comunes del conocimiento y la cultura y una expresión del colonialismo digital, que afecta especialmente a la Mayoría Global.

title: Bangladesh: Proposed changes to cyber laws risk granting authorities excessive power to police online content
content:
New proposed amendments to Bangladesh’s laws on online speech would give authorities wide-ranging and arbitrary powers to police content and restrict the right to freedom of expression, Amnesty International said today.

The new draft Cyber Protection (Amendment) Act, 2026 would grant government agencies overly broad powers to remove, block, or relocate any online content deemed to fall within a range of broadly defined categories that do not constitute legitimate reasons to restrict the right to freedom of expression under international human rights law. These include content that “undermines” the integrity, dignity […] of the country”, or content that is “likely to create religious or communal hatred”. The lowering of the threshold for removal or blocking to content which ‘is likely to’ undermine security or create religious or communal hatred is vague and speculative.

title: We Need a Third Reconstruction: Bishop William Barber Pushes Democrats to Take Action After Midterms
content:
With Democrats preparing to take control of both houses of Congress in January, Bishop William Barber of Repairers of the Breach argues the coalition that delivered the Democrats their midterm victories must now hold the incoming Congress accountable and keep organizing from the ground up. He and other faith leaders are calling on members of the incoming Congress to join them outside the U.S. Capitol next month to sign “A Pledge for Moral Defiance” — a commitment to pass legislation that addresses the needs of poor and working people and other vulnerable communities. Barber is pushing for what he describes as a Third Reconstruction: a sweeping moral and political agenda that includes a living wage, universal healthcare, protecting voting rights, affordable housing, environmental justice and comprehensive immigration reform.

“This was a vote not for Democrats,” says Barber. “It was a vote to say, 'Will you use policy to answer the pain that we are experiencing in this country at this particular moment?'”

title: Ei pirstaloitumiselle – Etla ehdottaa uuden EU-rahoituksen kohdentamista tekoälyinfraan, soteen ja puolustukseen
content:
Euroopan unionin uusi rahoituskehys voisi tarjota Suomelle liki viiden miljardin euron potin, kun mukaan lasketaan kansallinen vastinrahoitus. Etlan tuoreen muistion mukaan uusi rahoituskehys avaa myös Suomelle tilaisuuden uudistua. Rahoitus tulisi keskittää sellaisiin investointeihin ja uudistuksiin, jotka uhkaavat muuten jäädä toteuttamatta julkisen talouden tiukassa tilanteessa. Mahdollisia kohteita ovat Etlan mukaan muun muassa julkisen sektorin tekoäly- ja datainfrastruktuuri, sote-uudistus, puhdas teollisuus sekä puolustus ja varautuminen. Sääntöjen luoma liikkumavara ei muuta julkisen talouden budjettirajoitteita. Kyseessä ei ole ilmainen raha vaan julkisen rahoituksen tulee perustua tunnistettavaan tarpeeseen.

Euroopan komission ehdotus unionin vuosien 2028–2034 monivuotiseksi rahoituskehykseksi muuttaisi toteutuessaan EU-rahan käyttöä merkittävästi nykyisestä. Korvamerkittyä rahoitusta olisi aiempaa vähemmän, mutta jäsenvaltioiden harkintaan jäävää rahoitusta puolestaan enemmän. Suomelle voisi kohdistua arviolta 4,5–5,5 miljardia euroa, kun mukaan luetaan myös kansallinen vastinrahoitus.

title: COP31 Failed Climate-Displaced Communities
content:
Leaving the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, I can’t shake the disconnect between the reality of entire communities losing their homes to rising seas and some governments’ apathy and obstruction of the process. The conference ended without consensus on the proposed Antalya Pact—the overarching political agreement for the COP31 climate summit.

I am still in awe of Francis, a community leader from Solomon Islands who traveled to Antalya to share his story. “Walande… the birthplace written in my passport, no longer exists,” he told a hushed room. “It is submerged beneath the waves.” His words moved the high-level event’s moderator to tears.

title: Behold the Most Detailed Painting in History: The Ghent Altarpiece
content:
These days, if you want to see a particular painting, you can almost certainly pull it up online in seconds. In more and more cases, the resolution of the image will be so high that you can zoom in and in and in: such a level of detail is unavailable in a museum, of course, but also difficult to access even if you owned the physical artwork in question. Here on Open Culture, we’ve previously featured such luxuriantly digitized paintings as The Night Watch, Girl with a Pearl Earring, and The Garden of Earthly Delights. But there’s at least one celebrated work of Dutch masters whose viewing experience can never truly be replicated on the internet: the Ghent Altarpiece, also called the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, by Hubert and Jan van Eyck.

After watching the video from The Gaze above, you’ll surely want to take as close as possible a look at the online Ghent Altarpiece, seeking out such highlighted details as the individual hairs on Adam’s beard, the realistically awkward expressions on the faces of the angel chorus, and the identifiable crucifixion scene pinned to a pilgrim’s hat.

title: More than 99 per cent of Gaza shows indicators of environmental contamination from Israel’s military assault
content:
Israel's destruction of Gaza through the extensive use of explosive and incendiary weapons has made air, soil and water dangerous to Palestinians now and for decades to come, with indicators of toxic contamination across almost the entirety of the Strip. 

New analyses in a report released by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (CEOBS) today, has found that Israel’s military assault has created widespread contamination risks across Gaza, with heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, dioxins and biological contaminants threatening the environmental life support systems that people in Gaza depend upon for survival.

“Environmental War Crimes: How Israel’s military assault has turned Gaza into a toxic wasteland, threatening human survival” found that the scale and intensity of the Israeli military’s onslaught has affected approximately 78 per cent of Gaza’s land area, with the report’s spatial analysis identifying indicators of potential contamination across more than 99 per cent of the territory; highlighting the scale and near-total geographical spread of pollution risks.

title: Miten kehitysyhteistyö eroaa hätäavusta?
content:
Kehitysyhteistyö eroaa hätäavusta siinä, että sen tavoitteena ei ole tarjota tilapäistä helpotusta vaan rakentaa pysyviä rakenteita, jotka mahdollistavat yhteisöjen oman kehityksen. Hätäapu eli humanitaarinen apu vastaa välittömään tarpeeseen, kun taas kehitysyhteistyö kysyy, miksi tuo tarve on olemassa ja miten se poistetaan pysyvästi. Alla käymme läpi kehitysyhteistyön keskeisimmät kysymykset yksityishenkilöiden ja yritysten näkökulmasta.

Kehitysyhteistyö on pitkäjänteistä toimintaa, jossa tuetaan haavoittuvien yhteisöjen omia voimavaroja koulutuksen, toimeentulon ja rauhan rakentamisen kautta. Se ei ole avun antamista ulkoapäin vaan kumppanuutta, jossa paikalliset yhteisöt ovat aktiivisia toimijoita omassa kehityksessään.

Käytännössä kehitysyhteistyö voi tarkoittaa esimerkiksi sitä, että konflikteista kärsivillä alueilla varmistetaan lasten mahdollisuus käydä koulua, tuetaan paikallisia yrittäjiä luomaan kestävä toimeentulo tai vahvistetaan yhteisöjen kykyä ratkaista konflikteja rauhanomaisesti. Toiminta suunnitellaan yhdessä paikallisten kumppanien kanssa, jotta tulokset vastaavat todellisiin tarpeisiin eivätkä ulkopuolisten oletuksiin.

title: Sápmái Buorrin käynnisti pilottikaupunkialoitteen Levillä pujottelun maailmancupin yhteydessä 13.–15.11.2026
Even horse breeds are subject to human bias: here’s why
content:
Hello, I’m Tsaag Valren, and those who know me know that I mostly contribute to Wikipedia and Wikidata on the subject of horse breeds. I have already written about creating genealogical graphs and visualizing them on Wikidata. Perhaps that led you to believe that horse breeds are a 100% objective topic to contribute on?

Horse breeds are a subject heavily affected by human bias. We can start by asking this question: who decides that a horse breed is a horse breed? The concept of horse breed was forged in Italy, and later in England out of the breeding of the Thoroughbred in the 18th century. From there, you can guess that naturalists, English ones in particular, traveled all over the world to describe the “breeds” of other countries, even when locally nobody cared about the concept of breed. Sometimes, breeds are described in a way that matches the distinctions the riders and breeders of those countries make themselves. And sometimes, not at all!

title: Iraq’s Oil Minister Denies Ouster Rumors as Najaf Smuggling Scandal Widens
content:
Iraq’s Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair al-Abadi on Monday denied media reports  that prime minister Ali Al Zaidi was considering dismissing him following the discovery of possible oil smuggling operations in the Iraqi province of Najaf this weekend. 

"The issue of resignation is completely unfounded," al-Abadi said in a statement, adding that he fully supports the government’s anti-corruption efforts.

Al-Abadi’s reaction came after Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council on Saturday said a court issued arrest warrants against the head of the Energy Committee at the Najaf Provincial Council and his brother after an investigating judge conducted a field inspection in a plot of land belonging to the siblings.

The judge found “encroachment on one of the oil pipelines in the Najaf Governorate,” the statement said, adding that the two men “had previously dug a trench surrounding the plot of land on all sides, hindering access and preventing people from observing the activities taking place there.”

title: Costa’s EU budget cut meets chorus of doubt, reservations
content:
The proposed 10-per-cent cut has drawn fire from Paris and the largest parliamentary group. It has also earned scepticism from Berlin and the Commission, which welcome it as the “first step” only.

The European Parliament’s largest political group has rejected European Council President António Costa’s proposal to cut the 2028–2034 Multiannual Financial Framework by roughly 10 per cent. The group’s chief negotiator called the offer unacceptable. The EPP Group has 185 members from all member states.

MEP Siegfried Mureșan (EPP/ROU), the group’s vice-president, reacted to Mr Costa’s negotiating box. “President Costa’s proposal is simply unacceptable. The Council is fixated on cuts when Europe needs ambition and resources to tackle its mounting challenges.” Mr Mureșan went further. “The Council is moving further away from Parliament’s position. It must change course.”

He warned national leaders not to expect easy approval. “National leaders must not expect the European Parliament to rubber-stamp a budget that holds Europe back.” He wants a moderate 10 per cent increase, backed by efficient new own resources, including a digital levy that would make tech giants pay.

title: Working for nothing
content: How would you feel if I told you that, from today, you would no longer be paid for your work until the end of the year? For millions of women, this is effectively what the gender pay gap amounts to. Every year, the French feminist movement Les Glorieuses turns the gender pay gap into a date marking when women in effect start working for free. This year, the campaign celebrates its 10th anniversary. In France, that moment fell on 19 November at 10.51 – hence its #19Novembre10h51 movement. But what if we applied the same calculation across the EU? According to Eurostat, women in the EU earned, on average, 11.1% less per hour than men in 2024. Applying Les Glorieuses’ methodology, this translates into approximately 28 unpaid working days. On that basis, the EU's symbolic date would fall on 23 November 09.12. But why does the gender pay gap persist? Among other reasons, women remain overrepresented in lower-paid sectors, take on a greater share of unpaid care work – which can lead to more part-time employment – and have fewer opportunities to progress into senior roles. title: If They Call 911 About Domestic Abuse, Will They Be Deported?
content: About a dozen women chitchatted in Spanish between forkfuls of a tres leches cake. They spoke about their hopes and dreams — learning to drive, speaking English, visiting a son who had been deported. Some brought their young children, who scurried around them, circling the tables and tugging at their shirts, before the older kids nudged them into a nearby playroom, giving the women space to talk. The women were from Mexico and Guatemala, the Dominican Republic and El Salvador. Some settled here in west Michigan decades ago and had already become U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Others were more recent arrivals, with pending asylum cases. All of them said they had been abused by their current or former partners. And they had gathered at this informal support group, hosted by a local nonprofit, to talk.

title: OPINION: Who Gets to Design the Future of Food Systems?
content:
The future of food systems should be shaped with the people whose lives depend on them.

By Neena Joshi*

KATHMANDU, Nepal | 23 November 2026 (IDN) — Tara Devi, a smallholder farmer from Muzaffarpur, Bihar, India, understands what it takes to make a farming household more resilient. As a Community Agro-Vet Entrepreneur (CAVE), she provides livestock health services and advice to 700–800 families in her community. Her work connects smallholder farmers with the knowledge and services they need to protect their livestock, improve productivity and strengthen their livelihoods.

But Tara’s experience also raises a bigger question about the future of food systems. Who gets to shape the solutions designed to transform them?

The development community has become increasingly sophisticated at designing solutions for a more resilient and sustainable food system. Blended finance, catalytic capital, climate finance, technology, regenerative agriculture and new investment models are giving us powerful tools to address complex challenges. Yet, for all our sophistication, we still too often design for communities rather than with them.

The future of food systems should be shaped with the people whose lives depend on them.

title: Shrinking interest and divided trust: How Spaniards get their news
content:
Spaniards will soon head to the polls for a snap general election on 29 November. The latest polls suggest the vote is an uphill battle for the country’s centre-left prime minister. After being in power since 2018, Pedro Sánchez now risks being ousted by a right-wing government. The election is a good moment to explore how Spaniards get their news with the help of more than a decade of survey data from our Digital News Report. 

Our surveys show news use in Spain is divided across age groups, with younger audiences more critical, less interested and more likely to use AI chatbots and social media for news than older age groups. Both interest and trust have plummeted in the past decade, with trust in the public broadcaster deeply polarised along political lines. Many Spaniards are critical of climate and immigration coverage, and concerns about online misinformation are at their peak. Here are nine findings from our research.

title: How did the COP31 climate agreement fall apart – and what happens now?
content:
Two days after the COP31 global climate summit was supposed to finish, the talks in Antalya, Turkey, have come to an end – but not as we might have hoped.

Agreement simply could not be reached. The sticking point was the omission of fossil fuels in draft texts. The European Union led a revolt, shattering the consensus needed to adopt the cover text proposed by the Turkish and Australian conveners.

In a year of unprecedented climate disasters, a supercharged El Niño and as the world heads inevitably past 1.5 °C of warming, the EU and other nations said that the international process did not meet the moment.

Some coverage has suggested the rejection of the cover text is a sign the entire summit was a failure. This isn’t quite right.

These texts have always been add-ons to the formal negotiation process. Countries have regularly agreed these political, overarching statements, particularly since the Glasgow meeting in 2021, but they are not a requirement.

Its failure does not signal the end of the COP process – or the breakdown of the Paris Agreement. What it may mean is that international climate cooperation will look different from this point onwards.

title: Mali: Write for Rights global campaign supporting arbitrarily detained trader and influencer Rokiatou ‘Rose Vie Chère’ Doumbia
content:
Thousands of people throughout the world are joining forces to support Malian business owner and TikTok influencer Rokiatou Doumbia, arbitrarily detained amid increasing authoritarian practices in the central Sahel region, Amnesty International said ahead of the launch of its ‘Write for Rights’ campaign.   

Featured in the 25th edition of Amnesty’s global letter-writing campaign, Rokiatou Doumbia is also an activist who used TikTok to create a space where her 175,000 followers could speak openly about daily hardships and rising food prices in Mali, earning her the nicknames ‘Rose Poivron’ (“Bell Pepper Rose”) or ‘Rose Vie Chère’ (“High cost of living Rose”).

The 48-year-old influencer has two children.

On 17 August 2026, she was convicted and sentenced to ten years’ imprisonment for “discrediting the state” and “criminal conspiracy”.

title: "A Shameful Failure": U.N. Climate Summit Collapses as Final Text Drops Mention of Fossil Fuels
content:
The United Nations climate summit in Turkey, known as COP31, collapsed on Sunday after nations failed to reach an agreement on a new climate deal. A number of countries opposed the final draft because it made no mention of fossil fuels. Many poorer countries also objected to the lack of financial commitments from richer nations to assist them in adapting to the climate crisis.

“This is not about the Global South begging for assistance and help,” says Filipino climate activist Lidy Nacpil. “The principle is that [wealthy nations] have created this problem, and they have to contribute to the solutions.”

“What we’ve seen over the past decades is the Global North are not delivering on any of their responsibilities,” says Brandon Wu, director of policy and campaigns at ActionAid USA. “That’s what’s causing the deadlock. It’s not new to this COP, but it’s becoming increasingly untenable.”

We also speak with two other leading climate justice advocates who attended COP31, Tasneem Essop of Climate Action Network International and Kathy Jetn̄il-Kijiner, climate envoy of the Marshall Islands.

title: Small beginnings, big impact: how early-life care shapes pig health and improve sustainable production
content:
My research field is production animal medicine, with a particular focus on pig health, reproduction, and herd-level preventive medicine. I study how early-life conditions shape the survival, immunity, growth and welfare of piglets. I am especially interested in farrowing, colostrum intake and neonatal development.

Another central theme in my research group is intestinal health. We study how gut microbiota develops, how it affects growth and disease resistance, and how nutrition or management can support healthier animals. Much of my work connects reproduction, immunity, microbiology and herd medicine. The aim is to improve pig health in practical farming conditions.

Healthy production animals are essential for animal welfare, sustainable food production and public health. In pig production, the first days of life are critical. Piglets need a successful birth, the ability to stay warm and enough high-quality colostrum to survive and develop strong immunity. Later, gut health becomes central for growth, resilience and disease prevention.

title: Azerbaijan Further Tightens Grip on Civil Society
content:
Azerbaijan’s parliament on November 18 approved sweeping amendments to legislation governing nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) that would expand government powers to suspend and dissolve independent groups, impose new registration requirements, and further restrict their operations. The following day, a court sentenced prominent rights defender Bashir Suleymanli to seven and a half years in prison, the latest in a series of harsh sentences against civil society activists prosecuted over foreign funding. 

The proposed legislation would allow authorities, rather than courts, to suspend NGOs for up to a year for broadly defined violations, including failure to meet transparency and anti-money laundering requirements. It would also expand grounds for court-ordered dissolution to include activities deemed a threat to the “legally protected interests of the state and society”—vague standards open to abuse.

title: How Isaac Newton Lost $3 Million Dollars in the “South Sea Bubble” of 1720: Even Geniuses Can’t Prevail Against the Machinations of the Markets
content:
The Aristotelian notion of “man” as a “rational animal” has seen its share of detractors, from the Cynics to Bertrand Russell to nearly the whole of Poststructuralist thought. Leave it up to Oscar Wilde to compress the debate between intellect and passion into a pithy aphorism: “Man is a rational animal who always loses his temper when he is called upon to act in accordance with the dictates of reason.”

We no longer need clever verbal barbs to refute too-optimistic assessments of human behavior. Economics is catching up: we have the language of neuroscience and psychology, which consistently tells us that humans decidedly do not behave rationally very often, but are driven by bias and biology in inexplicable ways. And for over a hundred years now, we’ve known that the clockwork Newtonian view of the physical universe turns out to be a much messier and indeterminate affair, as does the universe of the human mind.

title: Ilmastokokouksessa myös edistystä – saastuttavien alojen maksut saivat tukea
content:
Vaikka Antalyassa järjestetyssä YK:n ilmastokokouksessa ei saatu päätöslauselmaa aikaan, solidaarisuusmaksujen asettaminen ilmastonmuutoksen tuhojen kompensointiin liikahti eteenpäin. Joukko maita, mukana Britannia ja Espanja, allekirjoittivat julkilausuman, joka koskee pieniä, kohdennettuja maksuja saastuttaville toimialoille. Tällä halutaan saada tietyt sektorit osallistumaan enemmän ilmastotoimien kustannuksiin, kirjoittaa The Guardian.

Saastuttaja maksaa -periaatetta edistävän julkilausuman ovat tähän mennessä allekirjoittaneet myös Kenia, Etelä-Sudan, Espanja, Itä-Timor, Tuvalu ja Vanuatu.

Vaikka globaaleja solidaarisuusmaksuja ei ole vielä otettu käyttöön, Ranskan hallituksen tukema työryhmä on ehdottanut mahdollisiksi tulonlähteiksi pientä maksua eniten lentävien ja bisnesluokan matkustajien lennoille sekä maksuja kryptovaluuttakaupoille.

Viime vuonna julkaistu hollantilaisanalyysi osoitti, että lentolippuihin kohdistuva maksu tuottaisi noin 106 miljardia euroa vuodessa. Maksu alkaisi turistiluokan lyhyen matkan lennoilla 10 eurosta ja nousisi pitkän matkan lennoilla 30 euroon, kun taas bisnesluokassa se olisi lyhyillä lennoilla 20 euroa ja pitkillä 120 euroa.

title: Waali and Dagaare Wikimedians Communities Organised Wiki Loves Food 2026 PhotoWalk at Wa Market
content:
On Sunday, 15 November 2026, the Wali Wikimedians Community, in collaboration with the Dagaare Wikimedians Community, organised a PhotoWalk at the Wa Market in the Upper West Region of Ghana as part of the ongoing Wiki Loves Food 2026 international photography contest. The activity brought together members of both Wikimedia communities to document indigenous foods, traditional ingredients and the rich culinary heritage of the people of northern Ghana through photography.

Wiki Loves Food is an international Wikimedia photography contest that seeks to document food cultures, traditional dishes, local ingredients and culinary practices from different parts of the world. The 2026 edition runs for one month, from 1 November to 30 November 2026, providing participants with an opportunity to contribute photographs that showcase the diversity of food and culinary traditions across different communities. Through this initiative, photographs of local foods and ingredients can be uploaded to Wikimedia Commons, making them freely accessible for educational, cultural and informational purposes.

title: pib – printable intelligent bot
content:
Werden Roboter uns ersetzen? Werden wir zu Konkurrenten? Roboter entstehen ja nicht von selbst. Erdacht, geplant und gebaut werden sie von Menschen, die darüber entscheiden, wie sie aussehen, was sie können und welchem Zweck sie dienen sollen. Doch was, wenn die Menschen hinter diesen Entscheidungen nicht jene Roboter bauen, die der gesamten Gesellschaft zugutekommen? 

Genau deshalb ist Open-Source-Technologie so wichtig, denn damit hat man die Wahl, Alternativen zu entwickeln. „Open Source“ bedeutet, dass die Baupläne einer Technologie öffentlich sind. Alle können sie als Vorlage nutzen, um sie zu erforschen, nachzubauen oder weiterzuentwickeln. Doch wer Zugang zu diesen Werkzeugen hat, trägt auch Verantwortung.  

Welchen Roboter würdest du bauen? 

Hier entsteht im Laufe der Ausstellung ein humanoider Roboter direkt vor den Augen der Besucher*innen. Alle sind eingeladen, mitzumachen und gemeinsam zu diskutieren, welche Eigenschaften Roboter haben sollten. Dabei lässt sich hautnah miterleben, wie dieses gemeinsame Vorhaben Stück für Stück Gestalt annimmt.

title: Ceasefire first, Brussels insists as Washington links Ukraine’s security to Europe’s
content:
Ukraine’s guarantees come with a condition: Donald Trump would support them only if they served America’s national interests. His negotiators now want to fold them into a much wider deal on Europe’s post-war security.

Talks on Europe’s future security architecture can only begin once a ceasefire is in place in Ukraine, the European Commission insists. Its position comes in response to a new proposal from US negotiator Jared Kushner, who wants to link security guarantees for Kyiv to a broader post-war settlement in Europe.

“Our position has not changed,” Commission spokesperson Paula Pinho said. “Those discussions need to take place in the appropriate forum, meaning with NATO allies and with the EU member states fully involved.”

Brussels also confirmed that it remains in regular contact with US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner over preparations for possible multilateral talks.

Mr Kushner set out the US approach in more detail in a post on X on Sunday. He argued that the two issues are inseparable. “Security guarantees for Ukraine cannot be finalised in isolation from post-war European security architecture. The two must be considered together,” he wrote.

title: Taking down the old Serbia
content: For as long as I can remember, Vojislav Šešelj's face has looked down over Novi Sad, Serbia's second-largest city. A giant poster of his head stood on one of the city’s central boulevards, despite years of protests and complaints. Šešelj leads the far-right Serbian Radical Party, and the UN war crimes tribunal in The Hague convicted him of crimes against humanity in 2018. He was also a long-standing political ally of Vučić's ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), and a prominent figure on the Serbian nationalist right since the 1990s. The poster carried a message denying the Srebrenica genocide. Despite an inspection ordering its removal last year, it remained in place. On the night of 25 October, as citizens celebrated the Student List's historic election victory over Aleksandar Vučić’s ruling SNS party, they took the poster down themselves. Scenes like the one in Novi Sad have become the new normal in Serbia. In the weeks following the elections that ended 14 years of SNS rule, citizens have been painting over graffiti, tearing down posters, and trying to clean up the country. But all this is happening before the Student List – a one-of-a-kind grassroots movement led by students

title: AlgaeFood: When seaweed finds its way onto the plate
content:
Innovative local food production: Offer someone a piece of seaweed with a “Bon appetit!” and you are likely to be met with a degree of scepticism. Until they taste it, that is. More often than not, the next thing you hear is: “That actually tastes quite nice.”

The seaweed that grows along the Danish-German coast not only contributes to water quality, but can also be used as food – unfortunately, this happens all too rarely! Because seaweed is actually a ‘superfood’ and it is a regional resource with great potential. Depending on the species of algae, the seaweed contains protein, minerals and vitamins – and it grows in the sea without requiring agricultural land.

title: “I’m not going to remove the repository”
content:
There is a hacking tool called ARTEX that is causing havoc around the world. It lets a hacker plug in their LLM of choice, and ARTEX will then spin up a bunch of AI subagents focused on different aspects of hacking, such as scoping out a target or stealing data. This tool can complete an entire hack of a target in just a few hours. The original author of ARTEX took down the tool in October after it became clear that bad people were using it. But, as I write below, ARTEX is free. Several people are still distributing it on GitHub. I spoke to them about it, asked them why, and for their thoughts about requests to take the tool down. 

And as I’m writing this, NVIDIA just said it has reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO, and Board Director. Hahahahahahahahahha.

title: French Bill Risks Deepening Police Impunity
content:
The French Senate on November 20 approved a controversial bill that risks deepening impunity for use of lethal force by police. 

The bill introduces a legal presumption of self-defense for law enforcement officers using firearms during the exercise of their duties, unless victims or their families can establish the use of lethal force was unlawful.

Because victims’ families lack access to key evidence to assess the legality of police-caused death, placing the burden of proof on them is likely to deepen impunity and seriously jeopardize pathways for accountability where lethal force was unlawful, unnecessary, or disproportionate. This is inconsistent with France’s human rights obligations with respect to protecting the right to life and use of force by law enforcement. 

The use of lethal force by police is a major concern in France. In 2023, a police officer fatally shot 17-year-old Nahel M., a racialized boy, during a traffic stop, triggering widespread scrutiny of police use of firearms.

title: Maailma tietää jo, mitä pitäisi tehdä – miksi se ei tee sitä?
content:
Antalyan ilmastokokous oli ensimmäinen sen jälkeen, kun YK:n ympäristöohjelma vahvisti, että maapallon lämpeneminen ylittää 1,5 asteen rajan. Silti lähes 200 maan neuvottelut päättyivät tuloksettomina juuri niissä kysymyksissä, jotka ovat ilmastonmuutoksen hillinnän kannalta keskeisimpiä.

Saudi-Arabia ja muut suuret öljyn- ja kaasuntuottajat vastustivat fossiilikirjauksia, ja torstaina julkaistusta päätösluonnoksesta ne putosivat pois. Dubaissa vuonna 2023 maailman maat sopivat ensimmäistä kertaa siirtymisestä pois fossiilisista polttoaineista energiajärjestelmissä. Kolme vuotta myöhemmin tätä tavoitetta ei saatu edes nimettyä Antalyan päätöslauselmaan. Tämän vuoksi EU ja useat muut maat kieltäytyivät hyväksymästä viimeistä päätösluonnosta.

Panaman ympäristöministeri Juan Carlos Navarro kuvasi tilannetta poikkeuksellisen suorasanaisesti. Hänen mukaansa "öljymafia" pitää maailman ilmastoneuvotteluja panttivankinaan.

"Olemme rakastuneet kidnappaajiimme", Navarro totesi ja vertasi valtioiden riippuvuutta fossiilisista polttoaineista Tukholman syndroomaan, jossa panttivanki alkaa tuntea kiintymystä vangitsijaansa.

title: Building the tools that help Africa tell its own stories: PULA at the WikiIndaba Hackathon 2026
content:
Building the tools that help Africa tell its own stories matters as much as writing the stories themselves.

As large as Africa is, we have so many languages to be poetic 🙂 Every story is told in a language, and every language leaves its own words: how they are spelt, what they mean, and how they sound when a typical African grandma with that language’s accent says them.

With technology, our stories travel more and more. Search engines, translation tools and voice assistants add to this progress, but these tools can only speak the languages they have words for, so if our languages, the pronunciations, the words are missing from the data, our stories will be missing from everything built on top of it.

This brings us to solving the problem, or having someone who has to put those words and voices into the data with the help of a tool that will make it possible. I never imagined I would be amongst the people or be that “someone”, and, funny enough, my journey into becoming a part of these started with a lot of doubt.

title: Thinking Through Motion – Exploring Physical AI with a Robot Dog
content:
Was braucht ein Roboter, um stehen, gehen oder tanzen zu können? Das Projekt Thinking Through Motion geht dieser Frage am Beispiel von Moby nach, einem vierbeinigen Roboter, dessen innere Abläufe sichtbar werden. Während Moby sich bewegt, zeigt ein Bildschirm in Echtzeit, was in seinem Körper geschieht: wie viel Gewicht auf den einzelnen Füßen lastet, wie stark seine zwölf Motoren arbeiten und wie sich sein Körper neigt und beschleunigt. 

Besonders gut lässt sich das beobachten, wenn Moby ein Bein hebt. Sein Gewicht verlagert sich, die drei übrigen Beine übernehmen die Last und die Motoren passen ihre Leistung an, damit der Roboter nicht das Gleichgewicht verliert. Auch der menschliche Körper gleicht bei jedem Schritt solche Veränderungen aus – meist, ohne dass wir es bemerken. 

Mobys Bewegungen gehen nicht auf einen einzelnen Befehl zurück. Sie entstehen aus dem Zusammenspiel dessen, was der Roboter wahrnimmt, wie seine Bewegungen gesteuert werden und was sein Körper tatsächlich ausführen kann. Diese Form der verkörperten Intelligenz hängt nicht nur von den Fähigkeiten und Grenzen seines Körpers ab, sondern auch davon, wie er mit seiner physischen Umgebung interagiert.

title: Did Coca-Cola bottler stop cheaper drinks from crossing EU borders?
content:
A can of Coke is the same in Madrid and Amsterdam. Its price may not be. Brussels wants to know whether Coca-Cola’s biggest European bottler stopped supermarkets from buying fizzy drinks where they are cheapest.

The suspicion is simple. Big supermarket chains operate across borders and want to buy drinks wherever the deal is best. The European Commission suspects that Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) may have deliberately made that harder. On 23 November, it opened a formal antitrust investigation.

CCEP is the largest supplier of fizzy drinks in Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, and Sweden. The probe covers drinks that people buy in shops to take home. Restaurants, hotels, and cafés are not part of it.

Investigators will check whether CCEP offered retailers discounts only if the drinks stayed in the country. They will also look at whether it sold different bottle sizes in different countries to make resale harder. Two more practices are under scrutiny: rewards for retailers who limited imports into Spain, and a refusal to negotiate supply deals covering several countries at once.

title: Räsänen: “Äärilaitojen talousradikalismi ei Suomea eteenpäin vie”
content:
SDP:n kansanedustaja Joona Räsänen näkee vasemmistoliiton vaihtoehtobudjetin esityksissä paljon hyvää mutta pitää vaihtoehdon talouslinjaa epärealistisena.

– Ripaus realismia tekisi tästä huomattavasti uskottavamman, Räsänen kommentoi Demokraatille.

Räsänen huomauttaa vasemmistoliiton todenneen, ettei sille sovi ensi vaalikaudelle kaavailtu noin 8 miljardin sopeutus. Samalla puolue kuitenkin esittää pelkästään ensi vuodelle 8 miljardin euron veronkiristyksiä.

– Jäi mietityttämään, että onko tämä ihan vakavalla mielellä tehty vai onko tässä oltu enemmänkin vaihtoehtomaailmassa, koska kuulostaisi aika rajulta, jos yhdelle vuodelle pitäisi tuollaiset vajaan 8 miljardin euron veronkiristykset tehdä varsinkin, kun heidän kevennyksensä eivät ihan yksi yhteen mene.

TYÖMARKKINAJÄRJESTÖJEN jäsenmaksun verovähennysoikeuden puolue palauttaisi tuplana.

– En ole aivan varma onko tätäkään laskettu aivan loppuun asti, koska sekä työntekijä- että työnantajapuolen järjestöillä olisi ilmeinen kannustin tuplata myös se jäsenmaksu, jolloin jäsenille ei jäisi sen enempää käteen. Veikkaan, että tämä ei ole ollut se tarkoitus.

title: West Bank: Israeli Authorities Harass, Arrest Activists Protecting Palestinian Farmers
content:
(Beirut) – Israeli authorities are detaining activists and community organizers attempting to protect Palestinian farmers during what the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) has recorded as the most violent West Bank olive harvest season in its 20 years of records, Human Rights Watch said today. 

Between October 1 and 26, 2026, OCHA recorded 397 settler attacks resulting in casualties or property damage, the highest monthly figure it has recorded since its documentation began in 2006. Israeli soldiers were present in 26.5 percent of such incidents documented by the Israeli human rights organization Yesh Din between September 27 and October 14. The Israeli military has detained hundreds of people trying to protect Palestinian farmers during their harvest, according to local media reports.

title: PELE – A Robotic Leg Powered by Artificial Muscles
content:
Im Inneren fast aller Roboter findet man Elektromotoren, die die Gelenke bewegen. Das Robotic Leg arbeitet ganz anders, denn wie bei den meisten Lebewesen sorgen hier Muskeln für die Bewegung. Seine künstlichen Muskeln sind kleine, ölgefüllte Beutel, die sich unter Spannung zusammenziehen und verkürzen. Sie arbeiten paarweise, ein Muskel beugt das Gelenk, der andere streckt es, genau wie unsere Oberschenkelmuskeln. 

Muskeln machen dieses Roboterbein zudem besonders beweglich. Auf Gras, Sand oder Steinen geben seine Gelenke nach und passen sich dem Untergrund von selbst an, ähnlich wie unser Knie, das wir beim Schritt vom Gehsteig unbewusst abbiegen. 

Während ein Motor Strom braucht, um ein gebeugtes Robotergelenk in Position zu halten, und sich dabei erhitzt, bleiben die künstlichen Muskeln kühl. In Tests verbrauchten sie nur 1,2 Prozent der Energie eines motorbetriebenen Beins. 

Derzeit ist das Bein noch an einer Stange befestigt und kann nur im Kreis hüpfen. Doch diese Entwicklung weist den Weg zu weicheren, leichteren und sichereren Robotern, also zu Maschinen, die weniger wie Motoren und mehr wie Körper gebaut sind.
