title: Poland Foils Russian ‘Mass Casualty Plot’
content:
For months, Western intelligence agencies have warned that Russia might stage a major provocation that could escalate into a grave confrontation with NATO. Poland now believes it has thwarted precisely such a plot. 

According to a November 18 investigation by the Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita, which cited unnamed senior sources connected to Poland’s security services, Russian intelligence was preparing a bloody false-flag operation near the border with Kaliningrad, the Russian exclave on Poland’s northeastern border.  

The plan was to stage an attack, possibly on Russian soil, causing mass casualties and planting evidence implicating Ukraine, with Poland portrayed as the base from which the attackers had struck. 

This aimed to drive a wedge between Kyiv and one of its staunchest allies, leaving Poles furious that Ukraine had supposedly dragged their country into a confrontation with Russia. 

Moscow could then have used the incident as a pretext to strike back, although it remains unclear where the bloodshed might have occurred.

title: Hungarian government moves ahead of EU directive with its own women’s rights reform package
content:
• Hungary’s new Tisza government has unveiled a comprehensive women’s rights reform package, marking a significant departure from the policies of previous Orbán governments, under which women’s rights advocates say legal protections steadily deteriorated.
  • Hungary plans to ratify the Istanbul Convention and strengthen legislation against domestic and sexual violence, leaving only four EU member states — Bulgaria, Czechia, Lithuania and Slovakia — that have not ratified the treaty.
  • The government intends to remove prescription requirements for emergency contraception, making the morning-after pill more accessible, although its relatively high cost will remain a significant obstacle for many women.
  • Hungary will ease its controversial fetal heartbeat decree, allowing women seeking an abortion to choose whether to listen to the fetal heartbeat rather than making it mandatory, but critics warn that the revised rules could still expose women to pressure from doctors.

title: How SNAP Theft Happens — and What to Do if It Happens to You
content:
When Kelly Joly swiped her electronic benefits transfer card at a Kroger in Beaumont, Texas, this August, she was trying to buy groceries for herself and her teenage son. Joly had worked for decades as a waitress. The day before her grocery run, she’d received her monthly $530 in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or food stamp, benefits, she said. But now, her EBT card was being declined. She tried swiping again and began to cry. The cashier told her that this had been happening a lot recently and suggested she report the issue. Joly stepped to the side and called Texas Health and Human Services as her food sat bagged up on the belt. 

The representative at the agency that oversees SNAP in Texas told her there was nothing they could do to replace the funds, Joly recalled. Her benefits were gone, likely stolen by fraudsters. Joly said her account showed transactions from the day before at stores in Illinois, Minnesota and California.

“I don’t understand why they wouldn’t replace [our food assistance] if they can see that it was fraud,” she said. “And on top of that, how am I going to feed me and my son this month?”

title: "Historic Judgment": World Court Rules Burma Guilty of Genocide Against Rohingya
content: The world’s top court has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the country’s Rohingya Muslim minority in a 2017 military crackdown that killed about 10,000 people and drove more than 730,000 refugees into Bangladesh. The landmark ruling is the first time the International Court of Justice has held a nation directly responsible for violating the 1948 Genocide Convention. “This is a vindication of what Rohingyas have been saying for the last almost 50 years, since 1978, when the first wave of genocidal expulsion was conducted by the very same perpetrating institution,” says Burmese dissident scholar Maung Zarni. By recognizing Myanmar’s “identity-based group destruction” of the Royinghas, he says, “the court vindicated [the] Rohingya’s collective articulation, memory and suffering.”

title: Satotilasto 2026: Viljasato tavanomainen, herneestä ennätyssato ja öljykasvit nousussa
content:
Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) tuoreen tilaston mukaan viljasato oli tänä vuonna tavanomainen, noin 3,3 miljardia kiloa. Viljoista rukiin sato jäi selvästi keskimääräistä pienemmäksi, kun taas hernesato ylsi jälleen ennätykseen. Myös rypsistä ja sokerijuurikkaasta saatiin tavanomaista suurempi sato.

Noin 1,2 miljardin kilon ohrasato on kuusi prosenttia tavanomaista pienempi. Sen sijaan noin 1,1 miljardin kilon kaurasato on neljä prosenttia suurempi ja noin 840 miljoonan kilon vehnäsato yhdeksän prosenttia suurempi kuin kymmenen vuoden keskisato. Noin 62 miljoonan kilon ruissato on neljänneksen kymmenen vuoden keskisatoa pienempi ja jää saman verran vajaaksi myös vuosikulutuksestamme.

Viljantuotannon rakenne heijastaa Suomessa enemmän kotimaista rehutarvetta kuin elintarvikekäyttöä. Viljan ruokakäyttö on vähentynyt lautasellamme ja ohra on lähes kokonaan hävinnyt.

title: CEPA Mourns the Loss of Ambassador Eric Rubin
content:
CEPA mourns the loss of Ambassador Eric Rubin, whose contributions to the cause of democracy and freedom, both within and outside government, stand as a testament to the power of thoughtful, dedicated public service. 

Across decades of service, most notably as US Ambassador to Bulgaria and Deputy Chief of Mission in Moscow, Ambassador Rubin brought unwavering integrity and deep diplomatic acumen to international relations. Throughout his distinguished career with the US Department of State, he served as a clear voice for democratic values while playing a pivotal role in strengthening transatlantic alliances and advancing regional stability. 

His influence extended meaningfully to policy analysis and strategic dialogue, including valuable contributions as a senior fellow to CEPA’s work. His investment in the next generation of leaders who benefited from his wisdom and experience made an especially valuable impact. Colleagues who had the privilege to work with him appreciated his warmth, sharp intellect, and collaborative spirit.

title: From FAIR to combinable and meaningful data: the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF)
content:
How can data from different fields be combined and understood by both people and machines, across different technical and scientific ecosystems?

To mark the 10th anniversary of the CODATA-RDA Schools of Research Data Science, CODATA and the GO FAIR Foundation (GFF) organised a session on this question in Trieste on 16 November 2026.

Here are the slides on the FAIR principles and FAIR Implementation Profiles, presented by Dario Bijker (GFF).

Here are the slides on the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) presented by Nina Grau (CODATA).

Sharing data is no longer enough. There is an increasing need to combine data from different disciplines and across different systems. This is only possible when data is accompanied by clear and consistent information about what it is and what it contains: its metadata. Yet each community describes its data in its own way.

title: Parliament has an AgoraEU deal. What did culture get?
content:
The article was updated on 21 November 2026 to reflect the budget figures in António Costa’s negotiating box.

On 19 November, the European Parliament’s Culture and Education (CULT) and Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs (LIBE) committees achieved a compromise on AgoraEU, the EU’s programme for culture, media and civil society for 2028-2034. The vote sets the basis for Parliament’s position in further negotiations with the Commission and Council — the committees voted to enter interinstitutional negotiations on the basis of the compromise text.

For culture, there is much to welcome. MEPs want to secure the Culture strand’s share of the budget, strengthen provisions on working conditions and simplify funding procedures. Artists facing forced displacement would have dedicated support. The biggest concern is international cooperation: the compromise would make it even harder to work with organisations from countries that do not participate in the programme.

title: Tule mukaan rakentamaan kirjastojen lukutaitotyön verkostoa!
content:
Hyvät ideat jakoon, vertaistukea arkeen ja uusia mahdollisuuksia lukutaitotyöhön – yhdessä olemme enemmän!

Lukutaitotyötä tehdään yleisissä kirjastoissa ympäri Suomen monipuolisesti ja aktiivisesti. Yhä useampaan kirjastoon on nimetty lukutaitotyöstä vastaava henkilö, joka suunnittelee, koordinoi ja kehittää työtä omassa kirjastossaan. Vaikka lukutaitotyötä tehdään laajasti eri puolilla Suomea, kirjastoalan ammattilaisille suunnattu oma verkosto on vielä puuttunut.

Nyt on aika koota osaaminen yhteen!

Suomen kirjastoseura kutsuu kaikki yleisten kirjastojen lukutaitotyötä koordinoivat, suunnittelevat ja tekevät ammattilaiset mukaan Kirjaston lukutaitoverkostoon. Verkosto on avoin kaikille lukutaitotyön parissa toimiville – työskentelitpä lasten, nuorten tai aikuisten lukutaitotyön parissa.

Yhdessä jaetut ideat kantavat pidemmälle

Lukutaitotyötä koordinoi kirjastossa usein yksi henkilö. Silloin kollegoiden tuki, yhteinen ideointi ja kokemusten jakaminen voivat olla erityisen arvokkaita. Toisessa kirjastossa hyväksi havaittu toimintamalli voi innostaa muuallakin, ja yhdessä haastaviinkin tilanteisiin löytyy uusia näkökulmia.

title: Building resilience for cultural heritage in the face of climate change: Europa Nostra contributes to SD-WISHEES conference in Tbilisi, Georgia
content:
How can research, international cooperation and civil society advocacy help safeguard cultural heritage from climate change? And how can evidence translate into meaningful changes in policy, funding and practice? These questions were at the heart of the international conference Resilient Cultural Heritage: Building Bridges between Research, Policy and Practice, held in Tbilisi, Georgia, from 10 to 12 November 2026, within the framework of the EU-funded SD-WISHEES project.[1]

Photo: Courtesy of SD-WISHEES

The conference brought together researchers, policymakers, heritage professionals, civil society representatives and international organisations to explore ways of strengthening cultural heritage resilience in the face of hydroclimatic extreme events, including floods and droughts. Discussions addressed the links between water management, climate adaptation and the protection of tangible and intangible heritage.

Vanessa Fraga Prol, Advocacy and Partnerships Manager at Europa Nostra, represented both Europa Nostra and the European Heritage Hub, highlighting the role of civil society, international cooperation and heritage advocacy in climate adaptation and disaster-risk reduction.

title: Tre sager i tovtrækkeriet om AI-musikken
content:
Må AI-virksomheder træne deres modeller på sange som ”Barbie Girl” eller ”Forever Young”?  

Mange musikere, pladeselskaber og rettighedsorganisationer siger klart nej. Og det er de gået rettens vej for at få opbakning til.  

I Danmark sagsøgte Koda for et år siden AI-musiktjenesten Suno for at have trænet sin AI-model på Kodas repertoire uden tilladelse eller betaling. I søgsmålet peger Koda på numre fra Suno, der ligger tæt op ad blandt andet Aquas ”Barbie Girl”, MØ’s ”Final Song” og D-A-D’s ”Sleeping My Day Away”. 

”Først og fremmest er det vigtigt at slå fast, at sagen ikke kun handler om Koda og Suno. Den handler om, hvilke spilleregler vi vil acceptere i AI-økonomien. Hvis tech-giganter frit kan bruge dansk kunst og kultur som gratis råstof til at bygge AI-tjenester, risikerer vi ikke bare at undergrave musikskabernes økonomi, men også selve grundlaget for fremtidens danske kulturliv,” siger Nicky Trebbien, juridisk og politisk direktør i Koda.  

Sagen er henvist til Østre Landsret og er endnu ikke afgjort. Mens vi venter på rettens dom, er her tre sager fra resten af verden, du bør kende.

title: Parlamentarisches Frühstück zur Nachrichtendienstreform
content:
2024 beanstandete das Bundesverfassungsgericht die Kontrolle des Bundesnachrichtendienstes bei der Inland-Ausland-Fernmeldeüberwachung als verfassungswidrig. Hierfür müsse der Gesetzgeber bis zum 31.12.2026 eine verfassungskonforme Regelung schaffen und auch bei der Kontrolle nachbessern. Ein umfassender Gesetzesentwurf für die Nachrichtendienstreform wurde vom Bundeskabinett im August 2026 dieses Jahres beschlossen und eine Woche nach unserem Frühstück vom Bundestag verabschiedet. Der Gesetzentwurf umfasste mehrere hundert Seiten, änderte zahlreiche Gesetze und warf eine Fülle von Detailfragen auf. Eine solche Reform, die Regelungen mit und ohne Frist zusammen verabschieden will, lässt sich in wenigen Wochen kaum umfassend prüfen, geschweige denn öffentlich diskutieren.

Zu diesem Thema veranstaltete das Bündnis F5 am 6.11. sein vierzehntes parlamentarisches Frühstück unter der Schirmherrschaft von Konstantin von Notz, stellvertretender Fraktionsvorsitzender der Bundestagsfraktion von Bündnis 90/Die Grünen und Mitglied des Parlamentarischen Kontrollgremiums.

title: Protecting Norway’s Gas From Russia
content:
In any direct confrontation, European critical infrastructure would almost certainly become a target of the Kremlin’s long-range strikes, as it sought to degrade the continent’s warfighting capacity and population’s will to resist. 

One underappreciated vulnerability in Europe’s economic system is Norway’s natural gas infrastructure. Since 2022, Norway has replaced Russia as the continent’s main supplier, delivering 89 billion cubic meters to the European Union in 2025, almost one-third of the bloc’s gas imports and more than half of its pipeline supply. 

Russia’s share of EU gas continues to decline, while geopolitical volatility is making several other non-EU suppliers, foremost the US, less attractive. Norway’s role can be expected to grow further, both in its share of supply and political weight. 

Dependence on Norwegian gas is particularly high in Germany, the continent’s industrial powerhouse, whose factories are critical to European rearmament. In 2025, Norway supplied 44% of German gas imports, and industrial customers accounted for 60% of German gas consumption.

title: Spain’s open-door migration model: A European alternative or a strategic dilemma?
content:
During the opening ceremony of the 30th Ibero-American Summit, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez argued that shared culture and values should translate into stronger political, economic and diplomatic influence. Against a global backdrop of increasingly isolationist tendencies, he called for a different approach: greater openness, cooperation and international engagement.

In his speech, he described Madrid as one of the hearts where [missing ending in source material] beats.

Sánchez recalled that the first meeting of Latin American countries took place in Guadalajara 35 years ago. It marked the culmination of decades of exchanges, connections and dialogue between the two sides of the Atlantic. He highlighted the cultural and linguistic similarities that unite more than 700 million Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking people. He also included indigenous languages in this shared heritage, emphasising the geopolitical significance of a common cultural community.

He cited Frida Kahlo, Pablo Picasso, Oscar Niemeyer and Antoni Gaudí, alongside Gabriel García Márquez, José Saramago and Rosalía, as examples of this shared cultural heritage.

title: The last good meal before the front
content: A warm bowl of borscht in a cold country, after a long day of work. Maybe that's what happiness is all about. I'm sitting in Trypichchia, a traditional restaurant in Kharkiv, a city about 30 km from Russian positions. And this borscht, I swear to god, might be the best I've ever had in my entire life. As a devoted enthusiast, I've eaten it in every possible setting: in fancy restaurants, at petrol stations, in village canteens, in shelters, and in trenches. I know my borscht. Mykyta, 29, one of the founders, tells us that the place started out as a local canteen at the beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion. Its sole purpose was to feed soldiers and volunteers who had stayed in the city when Russian forces were on the verge of capturing it. Since then, it has grown into a 300-sq-metre restaurant dedicated to one thing: “Serving the best food at the lowest price while rediscovering Ukrainian cuisine in a Kharkiv that has been Russified for far too long.” And you can feel it. title: The U.S. Paid Insurers Billions to Cover Civilians Harmed in War. Even the Government Says the System Is Ripe for Fraud.
content:
It was supposed to be a safety net for the workers who helped the United States fight its wars — a federal program that provided healthcare and financial support to the employees of government contractors injured or killed in Iraq and Afghanistan.

Instead, a handful of America’s insurance companies have become its biggest beneficiaries. While reaping billions in government payments, they have delayed care for legitimate injuries and received reimbursements for fraudulent claims, a ProPublica investigation found.

Over the past decade, American taxpayers have paid nearly $5 billion to insurers through the obscure program, which the government itself has described as “ripe for potential fraud or, at the very least, gamesmanship for profit,” according to an internal memo ProPublica obtained.

Nobody knows the true amount of misspent money. The official who oversaw the program under the Biden administration estimated that between $100 to $150 million is being wasted annually. The money has poured from a forgotten system for forgotten people who suffered forgotten injuries and deaths in America’s wars.

title: Finnish Institute of International Affairs launches FIIA Brussels to connect Finnish research with European policy debates
content:
As of January 2027, FIIA Brussels will host expert exchanges and policy discussions on European foreign policy, security and international affairs. 

Europe faces fundamental questions about its ability to respond to geopolitical, economic and other global challenges. To contribute to these debates, the Finnish Institute of International Affairs is bringing its broad research expertise closer to European policymaking through FIIA Brussels.  

Demand for Finnish expertise in Brussels has grown in recent years, driven by Finland’s NATO accession and the increased interest in the Nordic-Baltic region and in Finland’s comprehensive security model. FIIA Brussels provides a platform for dialogue and cooperation between Finnish and European researchers, experts and policymakers, to discuss these and other major questions facing Europe. 

“Brussels is the heart of EU, NATO and broader European policymaking. With FIIA Brussels, we want to bring our research closer to European policymakers, contribute to important debates concerning the future of Europe and strengthen the connections between European policymaking and our research in Finland,” says Niklas Helwig, Head of FIIA Brussels.

title: Soome Instituudi SA esinaise Marika Tammeaidi kõne instituudi 35. aastapäeval
content:
Arvoisa suurlähettiläs, instituutin johtaja, ja kaikki paikalla olevat entiset johtajat, hyvät yhteistyökumppanit, hyvä juhlaväki,

Suomen Viron-instituutti perustettiin vuonna 1991 – samana vuonna, jona Viro palasi itsenäisten valtioiden joukkoon. Harvalla kulttuurilaitoksella on yhtä painava syntymävuosi.

Instituutin toiminnan juuret ovat kuitenkin paljon vanhemmat. Voidaan sanoa, että ne ulottuvat vuoteen 1535. Silloin Wittenbergissä, Hans Lufftin kirjapainossa, painettiin Wanradtin ja Koellin katekismus – vanhin säilynyt katkelma vironkielistä tekstiä. Vuotta myöhemmin samaan kaupunkiin saapui nuori mies Pernajasta, Mikael Agricola, opiskelemaan Lutherin ja Melanchthonin johdolla. Hänen aapisensa ilmestyi vuonna 1543.

Ja tarinalla on jatkoa: Agricolan ainoa poika Kristian päätyi aikanaan Tallinnaan piispaksi.

Kirjoitettu viro ja kirjoitettu suomi ovat siis luokkatovereita. Ne kävivät koulunsa samassa saksalaisessa pikkukaupungissa, saman ajatuksen innoittamina: ihmisellä on oikeus kuulla tärkeimmät asiat omalla kielellään.

title: Judge gets First Amendment wrong in greenlighting Trump’s NYT lawsuit
content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:

New York, Nov. 19, 2026 — A federal judge today allowed parts of President Donald Trump’s defamation lawsuit against The New York Times, its reporters, and publisher Penguin Random House to proceed. Although other claims were thrown out, U.S. District Judge Steven Merryday declined to dismiss claims that the Times defamed Trump by, according to Merryday, suggesting he and his relatives committed tax crimes.

The judge acknowledged the Times had consulted with numerous experts on tax law, but questioned whether the expert opinions they obtained were sufficiently formal and detailed.

title: Family stories keep alive Georgia’s democratic past and the memory of Soviet repression
content:
In the Guria region, an organization is helping people recover a history the Soviets tried to erase

Resort in the Guria region of Georgia. Photo by Tinari.totoro on Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0).

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. Guria is a region in Georgia, situated in the southwestern part of the country. It has a coastline on the Black Sea to the west, which is about 22 kilometers (13 miles) long, and the region is bordered by the Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti region to the north, Imereti to the east, and the Autonomous Republic of Adjara to the south. title: Kenen etua kuvataidealan kasvu palvelee?
content:
Kuvaston puheenjohtaja Sade Kahra tarkastelee blogissa kuvataiteen toimialan kasvun suhdetta taiteilijan toimeentuloon. Puheenvuoro liittyy Uudistuva kuvataiteilijoiden järjestö –hankkeeseen, jonka tavoitteina on tiivistää järjestöjen yhteistyötä ja vahvistaa kuvataiteilijoiden edunvalvontaa.

Taiteen rahoituksen puolustaminen on tärkeää. Lisärahoitus voi mahdollistaa enemmän näyttelyitä, hankkeita ja apurahoja. Taiteilijan kannalta ratkaisevaa on kuitenkin, millä ehdoilla hän osallistuu niihin. Muuttuuko rahoitus korvatuksi työksi vai kasvaako toiminta kenties niin, että yhä suurempi määrä taiteilijoita tekee lisää palkatonta työtä ja kantaa itse suuremman taloudellisen riskin?

Edellisessä kirjoituksessani kysyin, mitä alan edunvalvonnassa halutaan muuttaa. Yksi tapa vastata kysymykseen on tarkastella kuvataiteilijoiden edunvalvonnan vakiotavoitteita, nimittäin pyrkimystä kasvattaa kuvataidealan julkista rahoitusta.

title: Maailman rikkaimmassa maassa viidennes on miljonäärejä
content:
Nobel-palkittu islantilaiskirjailija Haldor Laxness kuvasi teoksissaan köyhyydessä kituuttavia kalastajia ja lammastilallisia. Nykyiset islantilaiskirjailijat sen sijaan joutuvat miettimään, miten kirjoittaa maasta ja kansasta, jossa maallista mammonaa on yllin kyllin.

Islanti on näet maailman vaurain maa, ainakin mikäli on luottaminen sveitsiläisen investointipankki UBS:n Global Wealth Databook -raporttiin. Tässä vertailussa turvaudutaan vuoden 2023 julkaisuun, jossa oli vielä mukana suurin osa maailman maista; sen jälkeen UBS on valitettavasti rajoittanut katsauksensa paljon suppeampaan joukkoon valtioita, eikä esimerkiksi Islanti ole enää mukana.

UBS:n raportin mukaan islantilaisten mediaanivarallisuus on yli 413 000 Yhdysvaltain dollaria, lähes viisi kertaa niin paljon kuin suomalaisten. Lisäksi peräti 20,5 prosenttia islantilaisista on miljonäärejä, eli heidän omaisuutensa arvo ylittää miljoona Yhdysvaltain dollaria. Lukema on hätkähdyttävä, sillä esimerkiksi öljymaa Norjassa miljonäärejä on ”vain” kahdeksan prosenttia ja Suomessa kaksi prosenttia.

title: Are newsroom guidelines fit for purpose when it comes to data journalism?
content:
News organisations’ guidelines haven’t kept up with developments in data-driven journalism, they need to learn from practices in other fields — and principles need to be embedded in practice, according to new research on data journalism ethics.

Researchers Laurence Dierickx, Marilia Gehrke and Carl-Gustav Linden looked at dozens of European news organisations’ ethical codes to see how they relate to each stage of the Data Journalism Pyramid. They conclude that while ethical codes might talk in general about ethical principles, they rarely provide any guidance on how to apply those in practice when it comes to data-driven reporting.

Underpinning the research is the concept of ‘epistemic governance‘: the idea that an individual journalist is not solely responsible for the ethics of newsroom output.

This “governance perspective”, they write, “asks how ethical obligations become embedded in the procedural architecture of journalistic workflows, shifting ethics from values to be held to conditions to be built into practice”.

title: The most iconic sports film of all time taught us winning isn’t everything: 50 years of Rocky
content:
By all measures, Rocky (1976) is the most successful sport film of all time. Half a century on from its release, the story of small-time boxer Rocky Balboa – who rises to square up against heavyweight champion Apollo Creed — continues to capture our imagination.

Directed by John G. Avildsen, the film won the prestigious Best Picture and Best Directing Oscars in 1977. And the broader franchise, consisting of five sequels and three Creed spin-offs, has generated more than US$1 billion at the global box office.

Rocky resonates because it is the ultimate underdog story. The hero is flawed, yet faithful to his dreams – working to overcome his self-doubt. His final victory is not a boxing title, but in proving his worth.

The story of Rocky, written by Sylvester Stallone himself, was inspired by a real-life match between heavy weight champion Muhammad Ali and Chuck Wepner.

Wepner was a little known boxer from New Jersey at the time. While he didn’t win the fight, he held his own, becoming one of few boxers in history to be able to knock Ali down.

title: Wikipedia Recognized as a Digital Public Good
content:
UPDATE (19 November 2026)  – Wikipedia and Wikidata are now a part of the DPGs for AI (DPG4AI) Collection, a curated set of six digital public goods (DPGs) that can be used for responsible and equitable AI development– tools that place the public interest at their core.

Together with the other DPGs in the collection, Wikipedia and Wikidata provide open tools and knowledge that local developers, civil society, multilaterals, and governments can use as building blocks to develop and adapt AI solutions to their specific cultural and socioeconomic needs. This is particularly important in low-resource contexts and underrepresented domains, since ready-made AI tools can be ill-suited for what communities require and they may  reinforce existing biases or inequalities.

title: Historic UN ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya is rare victory for survivors
content:
Responding to the ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), the United Nations’ top court, that Myanmar authorities committed the crime of genocide in their clearance operations against Rohingya people in 2017, Amnesty International’s Secretary General Agnes Callamard said:

“Genocide. This is the unequivocal finding of the ICJ. After years of denial, impunity and suppression of truth, this ruling is a historic and authoritative recognition of the atrocities committed against the Rohingya and a rare moment of justice for survivors, victims and their families.

“For decades, Myanmar governments and military authorities have denied the Rohingya citizenship and subjected them to an institutionalized system of segregation, discrimination and persecution that amounts to the crime against humanity of apartheid. They have confined Rohingya to refugee camps, burned their homes and villages, and committed widespread unlawful killings and sexual violence, including during the horrors of the military’s 2017 campaign.

title: Russian Indigenous Activist Daria Egereva Remains Jailed; Arrested After 2025 U.N. Climate Talks
content:
Human rights and climate groups are calling on Russia to release two prominent activists, Daria Egereva and Natalia Leongardt, who have been held in pretrial detention in Moscow for nearly a year, since December 2025. Egereva, a leading Indigenous rights activist in Russia, was arrested shortly after attending the COP30 United Nations climate summit in Belém, Brazil, where she served as co-chair of the International Indigenous Peoples Forum on Climate Change. Leongardt has worked for decades to support Indigenous rights.

“Right now all we are demanding is the release of Daria and Natalia, because they shouldn’t be in prison. You shouldn’t be arrested for activism,” says Viktor Suliandziga-Bagat, an Indigenous rights activist and representative of the Udege people from the Russian Far East. He is living in exile due to the risk against activists. “I don’t think I can come back to Russia,” he says.

title: IPI restrictions in medical device procurement: from early experience to the first review
content:
Over a year into the EU’s IPI restrictions on medical device procurement, early cases highlight challenges with the EUR 5 million threshold and the 50% cap on Chinese-origin supplies. The first review of the IPI Regulation brings these issues into focus for contracting authorities and suppliers.

The International Procurement Instrument (IPI) Regulation (EU) 2022/1031 allows restrictions on access to EU procurement markets to encourage third countries to open theirs to EU companies. This sits within a broader shift towards using procurement to advance EU strategic interests, also reflected in the ‘Buy European’ preferences envisaged in the Commission’s September 2026 proposal for a Public Procurement Act.

title: Outage Chaos: Who Turned Off All The Computer?
content:
It's been a tough couple of weeks for anyone trying to use email, fly, spend money, use an Apple device*, or do signals intelligence. Technical service outages are nothing new, but why do so many big ones seem to be happening all at once? Are hackers, AI, and international conflicts to blame? And what can we do about it?

Since most service interruptions don't make the news, it's hard to get a baseline on how often we see them happen normally. But after a major incident like the Microsoft cloud outage on November 12, any smaller disruption is more likely to become a story as part of a pattern instead of an isolated incident. We would have heard plenty about the Air Traffic Control problems anyway, but the November 18 disruption to the PlayStation Network might have gotten less attention. There might appear to be a spike or an upward trend in outages, but we can't easily verify that, and the increased coverage will tend to make it seem more significant and interconnected than it necessarily is regardless.

Per Brahe-priset tilldelas en lovande forskare vid Åbo Akademi vars fortsatta nära anknytning till akademin anses särskilt värdefull. Hon disputerade 2022 och har sedan dess forskat kring mötet mellan vårdvetenskap, teknologi och klinisk praxis. Prisnämnden beskriver henne som en engagerad och väletablerad forskare med en självständig vetenskaplig profil.

title: Työllistymisen kannustimet parantuneet selvästi – lisätyön kannustimissa yhä isoja ongelmia
content:
Kokoaikatyön vastaanottamisen taloudelliset esteet eli työttömyysloukut ovat vähentyneet alle kolmannekseen Suomessa viime vuosikymmenen aikana. Etlan tuoreen laskelman mukaan työttömyysloukussa on vuonna 2026 edelleen arviolta 49 000 henkilöä. Jos vuoden 2017 lainsäädäntö olisi jätetty voimaan, työttömyysloukussa olisi ollut peräti 171 000 suomalaista ja vuoden 2022 lainsäädännöllä 128 500. Samalla työttömyysloukun luonne on muuttunut: aiemmin loukussa olivat lapsiperheet, kun nykyään loukku on siirtynyt pienituloisiin toimeentulotukea ja asumistukea saaviin. Ansiopäivärahaa saaneiden työttömyysloukut ovat lähes kadonneet, mutta sen sijaan perusturvan saajilla loukkuja on yhtä paljon kuin aiemmin. Tuloloukut eli työssä olevien esteet pienten lisäansioiden tekemiseen eivät myöskään ole Suomessa vähentyneet.

title: Vieraana OLGA: Minä menen eteenpäin
content:
Viisi vuotta sitten Olga Heikkala, 26, seisoi helsinkiläisessä studiossa. Sydän hakkasi ja suu kuivui. Jännitykselle ei kuitenkaan voinut antaa enää valtaa. Nyt oli uskallettava. Sitten Heikkala sulki silmänsä ja alkoi laulaa, vaikka samalla pelotti ja hävetti edelleen niin, että hän meinasi pyörtyä.

Kun Heikkala lopetti, hän ei muistanut tilanteesta juuri muuta kuin jalkojensa alla olleen tummasävyisen itämaisen maton ja kahvin tuoksun. Ystävä katsoi Heikkalaa ja oli hetken hiljaa.

– Sinun on jatkettava tätä, ystävä sanoi.

Heikkala nyökkäsi ja teki päätöksensä. Hän ei enää väistelisi välttämätöntä.

Perämeren ranta, Tornio. Ne olivat Heikkalan lapsuudenmaisemat, joissa hän varttui kolmilapsisen perheen esikoisena. Perheeseen kuuluivat äidin ja isän lisäksi pikkuveljet Oliver ja Alvar, edelleen läheiset ja rakkaat.

Lapsena Heikkala vietti mielellään aikaansa sienimetsässä, mutta tärkeintä oli aina laulaminen ja esiintyminen. Vanhemmat kertoivat myöhemmin, että jo päiväkodissa Heikkala asetteli ystävänsä riviin ja piti heille tanssi- ja lauluesityksiä.

Unelma-ammatista kysyttäessä Heikkala ilmoitti topakasti ryhtyvänsä pop-tähdeksi.

title: World Court Finds Myanmar Committed Rohingya Genocide
content:
(The Hague) – The International Court of Justice’s (ICJ) landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is a historic milestone in their long quest for justice, Human Rights Watch said today. On November 19, 2026, the ICJ found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya during the 2016-2017 “clearance operations,” carried out by Myanmar’s military.

In the case brought by Gambia against Myanmar for alleged violations of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Genocide Convention), the court ruled for Gambia, with a nine to six vote by the judges, that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. This is the first time that the ICJ found a country responsible for committing genocide. The court also found that Myanmar violated other obligations under the Genocide Convention, including the obligations to punish those responsible for genocide and to prevent genocide. The court’s ruling is final and cannot be appealed.

title: The End Of Extraction
content:
In the middle of Norway’s Hardangerfjord, I steady myself against waves that jostle the floating metal ring that encircles an enormous fish pen. My burly host laughs as I grip the railing. He needs no such assistance. With one hand, he grips an oversized bucket of pellets; with the other, he launches a spray into the pen. The water ripples and an instant later a silvery-blue cloud of salmon bodies starts breaking the surface.

This little meal is just for show. Throughout the day, a giant Akvasmart feed system shoots an enormous cascade of pellets — a mix of grains, legumes, synthetic astaxanthin pigment and the cooked, pressed and processed bodies of smaller, scaly fish — through long pipes into the pen, where between 150,000 and 200,000 salmon are growing plump. Across all the pens of the facility, more than a million salmon are raised this way.

title: The Amazing Inventions of Ancient Greece: From Plato’s Alarm Clock to Ancient Flamethrowers
content:
“It’s a sunny morning in ancient Greece. Students have started gathering in the Academy, but their famous teacher Plato is nowhere to be seen.” The great philosopher has, it seems, “overslept and missed his own lecture.” The sun and the sound of early-rising animals may have failed Plato that day, as the story goes, but never would he let it happen again — at least after he got the mechanism worked out for the first alarm clock in history. Its design involves a series of containers linked by pipes through which water flows at a steady speed all night long. When the water accumulates in the penultimate, sealed vessel, air is pushed out through the flute embedded in its wall, producing something like birdsong.

Plato’s water alarm clock is just one of the pieces of advanced ancient Greek technology explained in the new video above from Lost in Time, a YouTube channel whose look at ancient Roman technology we posted here on Open Culture last year.

title: How to watch the UK-EU summit like a pro
content:
BRUSSELS — Andy Burnham has gone big on Britain’s relationship with the EU during the first months of his premiership.

By the weekend, he may actually have something to show for it.

The British prime minister is heading to Brussels on Friday for his first U.K.-EU summit. But on the eve of the meeting, what exactly he’ll be coming back with is still up in the air. 

POLITICO analyzed leaked draft communiqués and spoke to diplomats and officials on both sides of the talks to piece together how the agreements are shaping up — and what’s still to be decided.  

Here’s what you need to know.

The U.K. and EU have committed to holding annual summits to build on the relationship they were left with after Brexit.

This is the second such meeting, and is primarily about concluding negotiations on agreements announced at the first gathering back in May 2025.  

That summit was attended by then-British Prime Minister Keir Starmer. This week’s meeting was originally due to be held in July, but it was postponed after Starmer stepped down — to give Burnham time to put his stamp on the process.

Three new international agreements are set to be announced at the meeting.

title: Avhandling om oavsiktliga graviditeter undersöker normer om moderskap och reproduktivt ansvar
content:
Ansvaret för att skydda sig mot att bli gravid anses fortfarande främst vila på kvinnans axlar. Lina Metsämäki disputerar i nordisk folkloristik vid Åbo Akademi med en avhandling om oavsiktliga graviditeter.

Det har gjorts mycket forskning om erfarenheter av abort men det saknas kulturvetenskaplig forskning kring situationen som föregår en eventuell abort, alltså den oavsiktliga graviditeten. Lina Metsämäki har genom intervjuer och analyser av textmaterial, som nyhetsartiklar, kommentarsfält och myndighetsrekommendationer, undersökt hur kvinnor som blivit oavsiktligt gravida förhåller sig till normer om kvinnlighet, moderskap och reproduktivt ansvar.

Några av de intervjuade upplevde den oavsiktliga graviditeten som skamfylld – fast de själva ifrågasatte den ståndpunkten som gammaldags. Ett vanligare sätt att resonera kring sin graviditet var dock att rama in den som något som kan hända vem som helst.

– Men denna förståelse förutsatte att de hade vidtagit åtgärder för att skydda sig mot en graviditet. Då kunde graviditeten förstås som en olycklig slump. Om kvinnan däremot inte hade skyddat sig var det svårare att framställa sig som moralisk.

title: Vihreät haastaa hallituksen talouslinjan – luontohaitoille hintalappu ja koulutukseen 807 miljoonaa lisää
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Vihreät julkisti torstaina vaihtoehtobudjettinsa vuodelle 2027. Siinä vihreät esittää mittavia panostuksia luonnonsuojeluun, koulutukseen, ja sosiaaliturvaan. Puolueen vaihtoehdossa ympäristöhaittoja verotettaisiin nykyistä enemmän, ympäristölle haitallisia yritystukia karsittaisiin ja hallituksen tekemiä leikkauksia peruttaisiin.

Vaihtoehtobudjetin rahoitus perustuu yhteensä noin 3,64 miljardin euron julkista taloutta vahvistaviin toimiin. Vastaavasti puolue esittää samansuuruisia menolisäyksiä ja verotuloja vähentäviä toimia. Näin budjetti ei puolueen laskelmien mukaan kasvattaisi velanottoa hallituksen esitykseen verrattuna.

Ympäristölle haitallisten verotukien karsimisesta ja muista ympäristöveroista kertyisi 1,876 miljardia euroa. Muilla veromuutoksilla julkista taloutta vahvistettaisiin 1,055 miljardilla eurolla. Menoleikkaukset, hallituksen menolisäysten peruminen ja muut säästöt toisivat yhteensä noin 709 miljoonaa euroa.

Vihreän eduskuntaryhmän puheenjohtajan Oras Tynkkysen mukaan hallituksen talouspolitiikka on vienyt Suomea väärään suuntaan.

title: Just 15 kilometers from the border: school shelter is a lifeline for Horodnia
content:
FOR UKRAINIANS, SCHOOL SHELTERS have long become more than just the only way for children to continue in-person learning. They also serve as safe spaces for civilians during air raid alerts and emergencies – acting as so-called “Points of Invincibility,” where community members can warm up, charge their devices, and stay connected during prolonged power outages.

Shelters are also used for community and cultural needs, hosting concerts, performances, school assemblies, and academic competitions. It is truly a safe space that gives children the familiar and vital social interaction of childhood.

However, not all children in Ukraine have the opportunity to continue studying at school alongside their classmates. As Minister of Education and Science Andrii Butenko said recently: “82% of schoolchildren and kindergarten pupils are currently covered by shelters, but we should distinguish between shelters used simply to take cover from an enemy attack and shelters where learning can continue. Only 42% of schools can continue the learning process during an air raid alert, rather than just sheltering the children.”

title: Miten joululahjoitus voi auttaa katastrofin uhreja?
content:
Joululahjoitus voi auttaa katastrofin uhreja hyvin konkreettisesti: se rahoittaa ruoka-apua, puhdasta vettä, lääkintätarvikkeita ja turvallista suojaa ihmisille, jotka ovat menettäneet kaiken äkillisessä kriisitilanteessa. Lahjoituksen vaikutus ulottuu välittömästä hädästä selviytymisestä aina pitkäjänteiseen toipumiseen saakka. Alla käymme läpi tärkeimmät kysymykset, joita joululahjoittaja yleensä miettii.

Joululahjoitus ohjataan suoraan kentällä toteutettavaan apuun: ruokaan, veteen, terveydenhuoltoon, suojaan ja koulutukseen. Luotettavat järjestöt käyttävät lahjoitetut varat kohdennetusti humanitaarisiin operaatioihin, ja suuri osa varoista päätyy paikallisten kumppaneiden kautta suoraan avuntarvitsijoille ilman turhia välikäsiä.

title: ADD-forskere: Den offentlige sektor er ikke et samlebånd
content:
Af Sine N. Just, Alf Rehn og David Budtz Pedersen

Forfatterne er professorer ved hhv. Roskilde Universitet, Syddansk Universitet og Aalborg Universitet. De samarbejder i projektet Algoritmer, Data & Demokrati.

Tilbage i juni 2025 trak Den Digitale Taskforce for Kunstig Intelligens overskrifter med sin målsætning om at ’frigøre’ 30.000 årsværk i den offentlige sektor ved hjælp af kunstig intelligens (AI); dermed, lød det, får sektoren ’mere tid til det vigtige’. Nu har Netcompany udarbejdet et alternativt estimat, hvor det vurderes, at der er potentiale til at frigøre hele 90.000 årsværk, hvis ’alle offentlige ansatte bruger AI-systemer til alle relevante opgaver og med fuld effektivitet’, som det lyder i rapporten. Både det oprindelige målbillede og de nye beregninger bygger imidlertid på problematiske antagelser, der fører til deciderede fejlslutninger. Konklusionerne er forkerte ud fra en værdibaseret vurdering, uanset om man med ’værdi’ forstår kvalitet til borgerne eller kroner og ører på den offentlige bundlinje.

Vastauksessaan komission aihetta koskevaan kohdennettuun kuulemiseen CSC kehotti EU:ta:

  • Selkeyttämään ja laajentamaan teksti- ja tiedonlouhintaa (Text and Data Mining, TDM) koskevia poikkeuksia.
  • Yhdenmukaistamaan tekijänoikeussääntöjen täytäntöönpanoa jäsenvaltioissa.

title: Far-right extremist or Ukrainian Fighter? Disinformation rewrote the story of the Krakow attack
content:
Saturday’s events in Krakow triggered a wave of disinformation across the internet. Within hours, false claims began circulating about both the attacker and the circumstances surrounding the shooting.

The perpetrator was attributed radically different political views, linked to Ukrainian military formations, and featured in manipulated photographs and videos generated using artificial intelligence.

There were also false reports concerning the response of emergency services and the alleged absence of police officers at the scene. The misleading claims came from anonymous social media accounts as well as statements made in traditional media outlets.

The incident has also demonstrated how powerful and convincing artificial intelligence has become as a tool for spreading disinformation. AI-generated content is increasingly sophisticated, and in many cases it is difficult to determine whether an image or video is genuine without using specialised tools to analyse it.

title: Here, have some cancer with your smoky bacon crisps
content: The taste of smoke triggers memories of cosy firesides and tasty barbecues. Think smoked ham, smoked salmon, smoked cheese, and the less traditional smoky bacon crisps. Smoke flavourings are usually made by burning wood, capturing the smoke, and turning it into a liquid that can be added to food. But these smoky flavours may damage DNA and risk causing cancer, EU food experts said in 2023, leading to an EU ban on eight substances that came into effect in July for flavours added to sauces, soups, and snacks. And more are now set to be snuffed out: a wider ban on smoke flavourings in ham, fish, and cheese will land in 2029. The traditional method of exposing food to smoke and heat in a smokehouse oven, though it too can introduce some toxic compounds, is still allowed. The flavourings industry has tried, and failed, to fight back. Food flavourings companies Kerry Inc and Kerry Ingredients last week lost their legal fight to overturn the ban for three flavours they make. Kerry and other manufacturers have been trying to find smoky alternatives or evoke smokiness with herbs, spices, or salt, with limited success. title: Corpus Christi Started Pumping Groundwater at “Lightning Speed.” Rural Residents Fear the Consequences.
content:
Late in 2024, Corpus Christi, Texas, was desperate for water after years of drought. So city officials hatched a plan to tap millions of gallons of water a day from an aquifer that serves dozens of counties across the Texas Gulf Coast.

The city would drill wells — lots of them. 

Corpus Christi’s drilling frenzy alarmed rural residents, who worried it threatened their access to water. They mobilized to create a groundwater conservation district that would regulate drilling and, they hoped, limit how much water the city could pump. 

Then Corpus Christi officials came up with a peculiar idea. Fearing the residents’ effort could hamper the city’s ambitious plans to tap significant amounts of groundwater, officials asked a local entity to serve as its well regulator. 

The advantages: City Council members appoint that entity’s board of directors, and its staff is made up entirely of city employees.

title: In Moldova, teens are learning about democracy and elections through an app
content:
The app gives short, interactive lessons using quizzes, flashcards, and other easily accessible formats in three languages

Originally published on Global Voices

Screenshot of views of VotEDU on the App Store. Fair use.

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement. 

Moldova is a relatively small post-Soviet state with a population of three million people. A landlocked country, it has a long border with war-torn Ukraine and Romania; with the latter, it shares the same official language. The territory that is now Moldova was once part of the Russian Empire, and later the Soviet Union, and Russia has been meddling in its affairs.

title: Xi-Putin-Trump summit was heavy on symbolism, light on substance – and not exactly a Yalta II
content:
It was touted as a history-making summit of the year. Presidents Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping sat down on Nov. 19, 2026, in Shenzhen, China, on the sideline of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, for the first such trilateral meeting of the three leaders.

Going into the talks, the trio had much to dicuss: the ongoing war in Ukraine, Middle East conflict and the march of artificial intelligence technology chief among them.

But what did 90 minutes of conversation deliver?

As an expert on U.S.-China relations at Harvard Kennedy School, I saw a lot of style, but less substance.

The first thing to pay attention to is the symbolism of the occasion. And so much of what was presented in Shenzhen was about the body language of the three men, their interactions and what that may indicate in regards to how they view themselves in a potentially new global order.

And this was on show even before the leaders sat down. At the beginning of the trip, when Trump landed in Shenzhen, he was met by Xi. Meeting a foreign leader at the airport is seen as a special honor bestowed by the Chinese president.

title: High-End Furniture Marketplace AptDeco Is Taking People’s Furniture and Not Paying Them
content:
This article has been updated with comment from AptDeco.

Last month, Erin sold a $3,000 large designer table on AptDeco, a white glove high-end furniture marketplace. More than a month later, she feels like she’s been literally robbed.

“AptDeco sent three men to physically collect my table on October 13, and here we are on November 16, with no payment and no concrete explanation for where my $2,000 (after their absurd $900 fee) is,” Erin told me. “It genuinely feels like I’ve had something stolen from me.”

AptDeco is a Y Combinator-backed company whose entire purpose is to take the risk out of places like Facebook Marketplace and Craigslist for designer furniture resale. It advertises itself as “simple and seamless,” and says “we handle pickup, delivery, and payments,” and claims that it pays sellers “within 5-10 business days.” But over the last few months, people who have sold furniture on the platform say that AptDeco has sold their furniture and taken it from their houses, but hasn’t paid them. 404 Media agreed to only use Erin’s first name because she is still trying to get her money from the company.

title: Haiti: Kenscoff violence highlights continued risk of killing, abduction and other abuses against children by gangs – new research
content:
Children in Haiti remain at risk of killings, abductions, sexual violence and other abuses by armed gangs, Amnesty International said in new research ahead of World Children’s Day.

Amnesty International interviewed witnesses to the Kenscoff gang raid on 23 August 2026, in which 55 people were killed and 15 more were injured, according to a municipal official. The UN said at least three boys and two girls were among those killed. A further 67 people, including 13 children, were abducted, according to municipal data.

Witnesses told Amnesty International that the attack began when dozens of gang members raided various parts of the commune of Kenscoff, south of Port-au-Prince. They attacked people in their homes, shooting them and setting houses on fire. They looted belongings and shot residents as they tried to escape. They also attacked displaced people who were taking shelter in the Ark of the New Covenant Church and shot many of them.

Children’s lives have been devastated by these horrors

Scott Edwards, Director of Amnesty International’s Crisis Response Programme

title: "Defend the Sacred": Indigenous Activist on Climate & Alaska Native Mary Peltola's Senate Victory
content:
Democrat Mary Peltola was declared the winner this week of Alaska’s closely watched race for U.S. Senate, making her the first Alaska Native lawmaker elected to the upper chamber of Congress.

At the COP31 climate conference in Turkey, we speak with Aakaluk Adrienne Blatchford, an Inupiaq and Yup’ik organizer from Unalakleet, Alaska. She says Peltola’s win is a significant milestone for Indigenous peoples in Alaska.

“Having somebody represent us in such a large capacity with such a big weight on her shoulders, but still carrying that struggle with her as she continues to advocate for our people and our way of life, is monumental,” says Blatchford.

title: Workday kasvaa vahvana EMEA-alueella: yli 2 500 asiakasta ja lisääntyvä tekoälyn käyttöönotto
content:
Lontoo, Iso-Britannia, 19. marraskuuta 2026 – Workday, Inc. (NASDAQ: WDAY), luotettu henkilöstöhallinnon, talouden ja IT-toimintojen agenttipohjainen alusta, kertoi tänään vahvasta kasvusta EMEA-alueella, jossa pääkonttoriaan pitävien yritysten asiakasmäärä on ylittänyt 2 500 asiakkaan rajan. Workday palvelee monipuolista asiakaskuntaa, joka kattaa kasvuvaiheen organisaatiot sekä yli 40 prosenttia Lontoon pörssin FTSE 100 -indeksiin kuuluvista yrityksistä. Tänä vuonna uusiksi asiakkaiksi ovat tulleet muun muassa Smiths Group, SEB ja ACHM Hotels by Marriott. Kasvu heijastaa laajempaa muutosta koko alueella, kun organisaatiot siirtyvät tekoälyn kokeiluvaiheesta kohti teknologiaa, joka tuottaa merkityksellisiä tuloksia henkilöstöhallinnossa, taloushallinnossa ja IT-toiminnoissa – samalla kun ne säilyttävät liiketoimintansa edellyttämän luottamuksen, turvallisuuden ja hallinnan.

title: ‘Today the Truth Has Been Recognized’
content:
As the International Court of Justice in The Hague delivered its judgment on November 19 in the landmark case that Gambia brought against Myanmar for violating the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, thousands of Rohingya waited anxiously in refugee camps in Bangladesh.  

In the Jamtoli Camp 15 in Cox's Bazar District, many crowded around a television. About two hours into the reading of the judgment, it started to rain. But no one moved.

The court’s president spoke in English, a language rarely heard in the crowded camps where over a million Rohingya sought refuge after fleeing Myanmar military attacks in 2017. At 5:13 p.m. local time, a community leader relayed the court’s ruling in the Rohingya language to the waiting crowd, telling them that, by nine votes to six, the court found Myanmar “committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine State.” 

The crowd clapped and cheered; many were in tears.

“The Myanmar military tried to convince the world that we had lied,” said 58-year-old Monajat Alam, from Rathedaung Township. “Today, the truth has been recognized.”

title: The Psychedelic Animated Video for Kraftwerk’s “Autobahn” (1979)
content:
Ah, yes, “Autobahn.” From the moment the door slams and the ignition starts, prog rockers and pre-new wavers know a journey is afoot. Though Kraftwerk had already made three albums, and the band members still looked like well-meaning, bookish hippies, 1974’s “Autobahn” is considered Year Zero for the denizens of the Electric Café, the four German robots who made human music with machines.

This cel-drawn animation by Roger Mainwood was made in 1979 to promote “Autobahn,” after most of the culture had caught up with the song, and it’s now bopping around pop culture again. By that last year of the ’70s, Omni magazine was a year old, music was sifting through the shockwaves left by Bowie’s Low and Heroes, analog was flirting with digital, and the world was ready to drive on that long, electric highway.

Mainwood’s protagonist is part alien, part human, and he begins looking around in awe in his hip goggles, then sets off for a run straight out of a Muybridge loop, only to wind up floating, flying, sailing and swimming through a landscape indebted to Peter Max, Push Pin Studios, underground comix, and 1930s modernism.

title: Costa eyes tax on Big Tech to boost EU budget after Trump’s poor midterms showing
content:
BRUSSELS — António Costa is seizing on an enfeebled Donald Trump to explore levying a tax on U.S. digital giants to finance the EU’s next seven-year budget.

The European Council president is considering asking governments to back a tax on tech companies such as Google and Meta to boost the EU’s approximately €2 trillion budget and unlock a deal on its final size, according to four EU diplomats and officials. In the past years, there has been little appetite for such a tax in Europe for fear of retaliation from Washington, but the Republicans’ poor showing in elections earlier this month appears to have opened the possibility.

“The probability of trade threats from the Trump administration has been reduced after the results from the midterms,” said Siegfried Mureșan, the budget negotiator for the center-right European People’s Party.

Costa, who is due to present a revised budget proposal for 2028-2034 on Saturday, is pushing leaders to agree on it by the end of this year — before votes in France, Italy and Poland threaten to disrupt negotiations.

title: Hieno kuvaus kipuilusta sukupolvenvaihdoksesta kirjallisuudessa
content:
Eero Karisto

Coda-romaanissa on kaksi keskeistä henkilöä, menestyskirjailija Willy ja kustantaja Andy.

Kirjailija on romaanin epämiellyttävin henkilö. Menestys on noussut päähän ja nyt hän kärvistelee, kun aika näyttää menneen hänen ohitseen. Ei hän tosin nuorenakaan ihannekaveri ollut.

Kustantajassa, tarinan kertojassa, taas on aika paljon reppanaa. Sosiaalisilta taidoiltaan hän on kömpelö siinä missä toinen on itsekeskeinen.

Kirja liikkuu monessa ajassa. Päätasoja ovat 1980-luku ja nykyaika. 40 vuotta sitten muodostui kulttuuria harrastava ja tekevä joukko, joka sitten hajosi. Jäljelle jäi ristiriitoja, traumoja ja selvittämättömiä asioita.

Jokin kaveripiirin dynamiikassa saa aikaan sen, että siitä ei synny elinikäistä ystävyyden verkostoa. Puuttuuko keskinäinen solidaarisuus? Toimitaan selän takana, käytetään toisia hyväksi.

Ihmiset erkaantuvat teilleen, osa katkeroituneina. Menestyminen on tärkeää. Ne, jotka menestyvät heikoimmin, katoavat tehokkaimmin.

Nyt sitten eri syistä ihmiset vähitellen kohtaavat. Mutta kohtaaminen on monelle vaikeaa. Entisten ristiriitojen lisäksi paljastuu uusiakin.

title: EU transforms Frontex into a high-tech deportation command centre

title: Grand Theft Wage
content: Grand Theft Auto VI came out on 19 November. It's the most anticipated video game of the decade (the last GTA came out in 2013), reportedly one of the most expensive ever made, and potentially one of the most profitable. Some predictions suggest it could bring in up to USD 5 billion in global sales in its first week alone. Europe is a massive market for GTA. The game costs around €80 in most countries, but its affordability varies once you factor in purchasing power. A familiar pattern in globalised products, like a Netflix subscription. For both, Ukrainians get the worst deal. The hype over the past few days has been insane. Gaming is a world of its own, but GTA is one of those rare franchises that breaks out of that bubble and gets everyone talking, including the mainstream media. Some viral headlines have even warned of a productivity drop as employees call in sick to play, something dubbed “GTA Flu”. But as The Guardian points out, GTA Flu seems to be more of a media phenomenon than an actual economic crisis. Still, the fact that we're even talking about it says something about the scale of this cultural moment.

title: The Trump DOJ Quietly Intervened to Ink a Huge Payout to a Trump Golf Pro
content:
Top Trump administration officials intervened to help a longtime golf pro at Trump National Golf Club Hudson Valley secure a half-million-dollar payout from the IRS. A company connected to Trump’s media business also got a half-million.

The deal grew out of a little-noticed federal class-action lawsuit filed in 2025 by five individuals and companies. The group got $2.5 million after accusing the IRS of failing to protect their tax information.

The law permits a $1,000 payment to victims for each instance of an unauthorized inspection or disclosure of tax data. In this case, however, the government’s monetary settlement is 250 times higher than what the law calls for given the allegations. Victims can receive more money if they show actual damages, but multiple officials say such cases almost never result in payments approaching this size. These generous settlements have raised concerns because IRS Office of Chief Counsel attorneys were not consulted about the settlement terms, as is standard practice, according to people familiar with the case and documents seen by ProPublica.

title: Support Global Voices’ December Spotlight: Digital Communities
content:
Donate to our Digital Communities Spotlight issue, and get more of the coverage you value!

Originally published on Global Voices

Images via Canva and public domain.

Digital communications sparked new ways of forming communities: communities that spanned vast distances; that offered asynchronous interaction, innovative forms of constructing identities, and potentially enormous reach. These communities have provided connection for people who are isolated or marginalized, built powerful groups around both professional interests and unusual hobbies, and facilitated astonishing feats of knowledge-sharing and organizing, from Wikipedia to academic sub-field networks to hobby groups and fandoms.

But digital communities bring new challenges as well, from questions of moderation to questions of ownership. Almost all of them are built on the backbone of infrastructure owned by Big Tech — hardware at a minimum, usually several layers of software as well.

title: Myanmar genocide ruling is a watershed moment in international justice – with huge ramifications for other cases
content:
The International Court of Justice’s historic ruling of genocide against Myanmar on Nov. 19, 2026, will have significant consequences for the parties involved in the case – and potentially some who are not.

The Hague’s highly anticipated judgment in Gambia v. Myanmar is a major victory for Gambia, the tiny west African nation that filed a complaint with the court against Myanmar in 2019. It is also a major moment of accountability for the military leadership of Myanmar.

But as an expert in genocide and mass atrocity prevention, I believe the ruling goes far beyond these nations. Indeed, it is also a watershed moment for international legal justice that is bound to have important effects on the court’s other ongoing genocide cases, particularly the case of South Africa v. Israel.

Gambia’s case focused on actions that Myanmar’s military government called “clearance operations” in the course of its decades-long violent persecution of the country’s Muslim Rohingya minority.

title: Black Neighborhoods Are Twice as Likely To House a Data Center, Study Finds
content:
Developers build data centers in communities of color at more than twice the rate they do in white neighborhoods, according to a new study from researchers at George Washington University and the Center for Security, Innovation & New Technology (CSINT) at American University.

According to the study, “Redlining in the Age of AI: The Relationship between Data Center Locations and Race in the US” majority-Black neighborhoods have 2.2 times the odds of hosting a data center than a white neighborhood in the same state. The number goes up to 2.6 in majority-Hispanic neighborhoods and 4.2 times in majority-Asian neighborhoods. “As the share of Black, Hispanic, and Asian residents in a neighborhood increases, so do the odds that the neighborhood hosts a data center,” the researchers wrote.

title: "This Is Not Going Well": COP31 Draft Text Avoids Fossil Fuel Phaseout, Bets on "Magic Technologies"
content:
As we continue our week of broadcasts from the global United Nations climate conference known as COP31, we get an update on the formal negotiations from German activist Luisa Neubauer. The latest draft text of the key climate commitments that countries are debating has dropped language about phasing out fossil fuels, but it does include an emphasis on carbon capture and storage — a largely unproven technology that critics say cannot be deployed at scale to curb emissions.

“We have much better solutions at hand, like renewables,” says Neubauer. “This is not going well. We are not doing fine. And if anything, after this conference ends, we need people to take the streets and fight for more justice out there.”

title: Workdayn European Workforce Report: Työntekijät pysyvät nykyisissä työpaikoissaan tekoälymuutoksen keskellä – kolmannes pysyy, koska kokee olevansa jumissa
content:
BARCELONA, 19. marraskuuta 2026 – Workday Rising EMEA – Workday, Inc., luotettu henkilöstöhallinnon, talouden ja IT-toimintojen agenttipohjainen alusta, julkaisi tänään vuoden 2026 työvoimaa käsittelevän raportin, European Workforce Report. Raportin mukaan eurooppalaiset työntekijät pysyvät työnantajiensa palveluksessa pidempään kuin työntekijät muualla, mutta pysyvyys ei välttämättä heijasta sitoutumista. Jokaisella analysoidulla eurooppalaisella markkinalla kahden vuoden pysyvyysaste on korkeampi kuin maailmanlaajuinen keskiarvo 69,6 prosenttia. Kärjessä on Saksa 78,8 prosentin osuudella. Yli kolmannes (34 prosenttia) työntekijöistä Isossa-Britanniassa, Ranskassa ja Saksassa kertoo tuntevansa olevansa jumissa työpaikassaan, koska työmarkkinat ovat heikot.

Monet näistä työntekijöistä kokevat saavansa vähemmän tukea työnantajiltaan. Vain 54 prosenttia sanoo, että työnantaja välittää heistä ihmisinä, kun maailmanlaajuisesti luku on 59 prosenttia. Ja vaikka 75 prosenttia vastaajista sanoo tietävänsä, mitä taitoja he tarvitsevat menestyäkseen, harvempi (62 prosenttia) sanoo, että työnantaja auttaa heitä kehittämään tulevaisuudessa tarvittavia taitoja.

title: World Court Finds Myanmar Responsible for Rohingya Genocide
content:
(The Hague) – The International Court of Justice on November 19, 2026, found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya during the 2016-2017 “clearance operations” carried out by Myanmar’s military, in the case brought by Gambia against Myanmar for alleged violations of the Genocide Convention. The court’s ruling is final and cannot be appealed.

The following quote can be attributed to Maria Elena Vignoli, senior international justice counsel at Human Rights Watch: 

“The International Court of Justice’s landmark ruling is long-awaited recognition of the suffering the Rohingya have endured from Myanmar’s military. The ruling also provides a significant precedent for victims of genocide, and other grave crimes, across the world in their own quest for justice.”

“Myanmar should swiftly comply with the court’s judgment and end its oppression of the Rohingya. Concerned governments should strongly support the Rohingya and promote justice for atrocities, press Myanmar’s junta to comply with the judgment, and ensure the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar.”

title: The web is held together by volunteers. AI could tear it apart.
content:
BRUSSELS — Long before the fresh spate of hacks and website shutdowns, the inherent instability of the web was depicted in an internet-famous cartoon of a rickety tower propped up by a single small block.

Now a near-daily rhythm of outages suggests the supporting block may have come loose.

POLITICO revealed Thursday that internal services at EU institutions had gone offline after a major AI-fueled cyberattack. That came after service interruptions at U.S. national security offices and the federal aviation authority, global outages at Microsoft and a succession of internet-activated attacks on supermarket refrigerators in Europe.

Authorities blame the sudden wave of instability on the capacity of new AI tools to detect vulnerabilities in existing code and for bad actors to exploit them.

Interviews with more than a dozen cybersecurity leaders and those working on maintaining the internet show the scale of the challenge to keep the web up and running, in a world where the pace of finding vulnerabilities has rapidly and permanently accelerated.

title: We’re Publishing the Tariff Refunds the Government Has Refused to Disclose
content:
After President Donald Trump’s “emergency” tariffs were overturned by the Supreme Court in February 2026, the government began processing billions in refunds to importers, including many recognizable public companies.

The Trump administration has not publicly detailed which companies are getting roughly $170 billion in refunds or how much they’ve asked for. ProPublica requested the information, but U.S. Customs and Border Protection denied our requests. (We’re appealing.) 

So our reporters found another way: analyzing the financial disclosures of thousands of publicly traded companies.

Today, ProPublica published “Cash Back,” a database of figures on refunds for tariffs paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. The database includes 343 public companies for which we found mentions of refunds, amounting to more than $28 billion recovered or expected.

At least nine companies have disclosed that they are using their refunds not to pay back the cash-strapped consumers who generally covered much of the tariff costs through higher prices, but to give bonuses, according to a ProPublica analysis published earlier this week.

title: Elizabeth Holmes went from a startup darling to powerful seductress – these gendered portrayals profited investors
content:
Despite the countless books, podcasts, TV miniseries and documentaries, people continue to be fascinated by the fall of Elizabeth Holmes and her health-tech startup Theranos. We are now being offered a new insight into the founder through the much-hyped documentary, You Can See Everything.

The initial drama of the documentary takes places 34 days before Holmes started her 11-year prison sentence for investor fraud in 2023. In our research, we examined how Holmes was presented across promotional materials, tweets, talks and interviews over the ten year period from her initial appearance on the public stage in 2013 to the same period in which the documentary begins.

Valued at around US$9 billion (£7 billion) at its peak in 2014, Theranos claimed to have built a device that could run hundreds of lab tests from just a few drops of blood. Holmes and co-founder Sunny Balwani hid that the device could not in fact do what they said, leading to its 2018 shutdown and their convictions for investor fraud (and, in Balwani’s case, defrauding patients as well).

title: A New International Order? Xi, Trump & Putin Hold Historic Trilateral Summit in China
content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted his U.S. and Russian counterparts for a historic trilateral summit on Thursday, with the leaders of the three biggest nuclear superpowers meeting for about 90 minutes in Shenzhen. Afterward, the countries published a “peace declaration” that affirmed “nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.” The declaration also announced a commitment to increase petroleum production, called for reforms at the United Nations and urged the International Criminal Court and similar bodies to “not abuse their jurisdiction.”

While in China, President Donald Trump also had a separate meeting with President Vladimir Putin to discuss the war in Ukraine, though it’s unclear if they made any progress.

“It’s a significant post-1945 moment, which was the last time that we had great summits,” says Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at University College Dublin. “What is the most important takeaway … is an ascendant China. It was China that really set the terms of what was said.”

title: Männynjuurikääpää esiintyy jo harvakseltaan Pohjois-Pohjanmaalla
content:
Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) tutkimuksessa selvitettiin männynjuurikäävän esiintymistä Pohjois-Suomessa. Tautia löytyi kolmesta metsiköstä Pohjois-Pohjanmaalta. Lapin eteläosista tautia ei ole toistaiseksi löydetty. Löydökset osoittavat, että Etelä-Suomessa yleinen metsätuhoja aiheuttava sieni esiintyy jo harvakseltaan myös pohjoisempana. Männynjuurikääpä hyötyy lämpötilan noususta, ja sen odotetaan ilmastonmuutoksen myötä leviävän yhä pohjoisemmaksi.

Pohjois-Pohjanmaalta löydetyt tuhoalat olivat pieniä ja paikallisia, ja niissä oli vain muutamia männynjuurikäävän tappamia ja harsuunnuttamia puita. Tutkimuksessa oli mukana noin 30 metsikköä, joista kolmesta löytyi männynjuurikääpää.

Sienelle alttiiden puulajien joukko on pohjoisessa laaja. Männynjuurikääpää löydettiin mäntyjen lisäksi yhdestä haavan kannosta. Kahdella alueella sienen itiöemiä löytyi myös kuolleiden katajien juurista.

title: Startups call on Commission to salvage or scrap EU Inc proposal
content:
HELSINKI — The European Commission should withdraw and resubmit its proposal for a new EU-wide corporate law framework, startup lobby groups said, denouncing the current text as a “Frankenstein” proposal.

A position on the law adopted by EU capitals in October “weakened or removed some of the very provisions that would make EU Inc. a true European standard,” Startups for Europe and EU Inc. said in a joint press release.

Both groups pitched the withdrawal to European Commissioners Henna Virkkunen and Ekaterina Zaharieva, who oversee tech policy and startups, during a policy roundtable at Finnish technology conference Slush on Thursday morning.

They also sent a joint letter to European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen earlier this week.

The European Commission published its proposal for a so-called 28th regime, also known as EU Inc., earlier this year, to harmonize how founders can incorporate a company and reward their personnel, so that startups can scale more easily across the bloc.

The scheme was seen as a challenge to the U.S. state of Delaware, which is known for its flexible incorporation laws.

title: African glamour: the bold women who styled, wrote and read Drum magazine
content:
Drum magazine was an African institution in the 1950s and 1960s. Launched in South Africa, it would go on to publish five regional pan-African editions across eight countries.

Much has been made of the male reporters of the magazine, but a new open source book considers how women used it to shape their worldviews and opportunities. We spoke with media scholar Wanjirũ G. Mbure about Out For Glamour In Africa.

Initially known as The African Drum, Drum magazine started in South Africa in 1951, three years after apartheid was signed into law. The system of white minority rule would violently disenfranchise Black South Africans.

This was particularly evident in cities like Johannesburg, where large numbers of Black South Africans migrated from rural areas to work on mines. With little investment in housing and social services, they were forced to live on the outskirts of the city.

title: ICE Is Paying AT&T to Dig Through a Mountain of Call Records
content:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement is paying telecommunications giant AT&T millions of dollars to have AT&T’s analysts sift through mountains of raw AT&T data for a wide variety of investigations, according to an internal ICE document obtained by 404 Media, other procurement records, and experts who reviewed those records. Civil liberty experts have called it a mass surveillance program, and they say the data can include trillions of phone records and location data. 

The AT&T product, interchangeably called Data Analytics and Support Services or Data Analytical Services, appears to be related to an earlier surveillance program called Hemisphere, in which AT&T provided U.S. authorities at state, local, and federal levels access to AT&T user data. Though that program shut down, ICE is still paying for access to raw data under this new arrangement with AT&T, according to the restricted ICE procurement document obtained by 404 Media. The program likely affects more than just AT&T customers because the company connects phone calls for other phone companies, meaning non-customers are likely swept up too, according to a surveillance expert.

title: Why depth beats breadth in Europe’s hunt for an AI edge
content:
​​​An artificial intelligence (AI) system is judged on the job it does, not on how clever it is in general. For European businesses, that is an opening. For example, a pharmaceutical company does not need a model that can discuss biology. It needs one that can flag the rare adverse-event signal in its own trial data. An energy grid operator needs load forecasts built on its own network topology, not generic ones. A defen​s​​​e manufacturer needs a system that can verify a weld against its own specification, and say why it passed or failed. Each needs a system that understands its domain, works on its data, follows its rules and guardrails, and can be trusted to execute in a protected, controlled environment.

title: Accused South American Drug Lord Faces US Trial after Judge Rejects Motions
content:
Sebastián Marset, an accused South American drug lord, appears headed for a January jury trial after a federal judge in Virginia this week rejected multiple efforts by the defense to dismiss charges.

U.S. District Judge Rossie Alston Jr. on Tuesday rejected arguments from Marset’s lawyers that the Uruguayan national was being subjected to a vindictive prosecution and misconduct by prosecutors.

Marset’s defense team had argued their client’s Miranda rights, which protect against self-incrimination, were violated when agents from the Drug Enforcement Administration interviewed him without a lawyer present.

But the judge held that Marset had initiated some of the conversations after his arrest in southern Bolivia and was not coerced into talking with DEA agents during his expulsion to Peru and subsequent transfer to the United States and custody in Virginia.

The judge also rejected the defense’s “fruit of the poisonous tree” motion that asserted that evidence should be excluded because it was obtained improperly.

title: Europe and China 3 – The Coming Showdown
content:
This is the third of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe. 

The negative numbers began to cascade across European balance sheets as soon as China entered the World Trade Organization in late 2001.  

But the cost-benefit calculations were not equal for all Europeans. Some nations, such as Germany, initially gained from high-value exports and joint ventures. Others, like Greece and Portugal, faced a surge of low-cost Chinese goods and strategic investments by entities linked to the Chinese state. 

The Chinese economy was barely one-eighth the size of that of the European Economic Community before the People’s Republic embarked on its policy of “reform and opening up” at the Third Plenum of the Eleventh Central Committee in December 1978. By 2025, the relative economic weight of China and the European Union was almost equal.  

Together they account for about a third of world trade. In 1975, their bilateral trade was worth about €2bn ($2.2bn) annually; 50 years later, it was €2bn a day, according to figures compiled for the Institut Jacques Delors.
